objects.description: No custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. It only declares four constexpr integral constants within the Pistache::Version namespace. There are therefore no user-defined types to document.
Custom runtime_error used by Async to signal promise-related errors (e.g., invalid resolve/reject usages).
Error indicating an attempt to resolve a promise with a value whose erased TypeId does not match the promise's expected type.
Exception thrown when Async::Any cast<T>() is attempted with the wrong stored type.
Tri-state enum for promise lifecycle: Pending, Fulfilled, or Rejected.
Abstract base class exposing read-only state inspection for promises.
Internal helper carrying an exception_ptr to rethrow across continuation boundaries.
Policy functor that ignores a rejection exception_ptr. Used as a reject callback convenience.
Policy functor that terminates the program upon rejection. Useful for fire-and-forget continuations.
Policy functor that wraps an exception_ptr into InternalRethrow and throws it, propagating rejection.
Abstract interface representing a continuation request attached to a promise core. It receives resolve/reject notifications.
Type-erased shared state for a promise, storing state, exception, and continuation requests. CoreT<T> specializes storage and access for value type T (including void specialization).
Movable handle bound to a promise Core that fulfills it with a value or without (for void). Enforces single-settle semantics and notifies continuations.
Movable handle bound to a promise Core that rejects it with an exception (wrapped into exception_ptr) and notifies continuations.
Pair of Resolver/Rejection handles supplied to async producer code to settle a Promise<T>. The void specialization exposes resolve() without value.
Type-erased wrapper for any Promise value used by whenAny; supports type checks via TypeId and casting with runtime validation.
Policy used by When to implement whenAll semantics: waits for all inputs, aggregates results (tuple) and resolves once all are fulfilled; rejects on first failure.
Policy used by When to implement whenAny semantics: resolves with the first result wrapped in Async::Any, or rejects with the first error.

A utility class that decodes a Base64-encoded std::string into raw bytes (std::byte). It holds a reference to the input string and stores the decoded bytes internally. Methods include computing the decoded size, performing the decode, and accessing the decoded buffer. Construction requires a reference to an existing Base64 string that must outlive the decoder instance. DecodeCharacter maps a single base64 character to its 6-bit value; error handling details are not exposed here.

A utility class that encodes raw bytes (std::vector<std::byte>) into a Base64 string. It holds a reference to the input buffer, provides size estimation, performs the encoding, and returns or exposes the resulting Base64 string. The referenced input buffer must outlive the encoder instance. Includes a static helper to encode an std::string directly.

For pre-C++17 environments, defines std::byte as an alias of uint8_t within namespace std. In C++17 and later, this block is inactive and the standard std::byte is used. This provides a byte-sized enumeration-like type for raw byte operations.

A callable functor that takes a std::exception_ptr and prints the contained exception’s what() message to std::cerr. Useful as a generic exception handler for asynchronous contexts (e.g., futures, thread pools). No state is stored and no ownership semantics apply.

HTTP cookie representation following RFC 6265. Holds cookie name/value, optional attributes (path, domain, expires, maxAge), flags (secure, httpOnly), and extension attributes. Provides parsing helpers from raw header strings and stream output via operator<<. Constructor requires name and value.
direct_api_constructors: Pistache::Http::Cookie Pistache::Http::Cookie::fromRaw(const char* str, size_t len)

objects.description: Container and manager for HTTP cookies. Internally stores cookies in a two-level unordered_map keyed by name, then by value. Supports adding cookies (including parsing from raw header strings), retrieving by name, presence checks, iteration via custom iterator, and clearing all cookies.

Forward-iterating adaptor over CookieJar’s nested storage. Provides bidirectional iterator_category typedef but defines pre/post-increment and equality/inequality; dereferences to a Cookie by value and provides pointer-like access to the contained Cookie. Iterates across inner maps and advances to next bucket when needed. Note: returns Cookie by value on operator*, so modifications through the iterator do not affect storage.

objects.definition: typedef std::int32_t Integer;
objects.description: Alias for 32-bit signed integer used as a Swagger data type.

objects.definition: typedef std::int64_t Long;
objects.description: Alias for 64-bit signed integer Swagger data type.

objects.definition: typedef float Float;
objects.description: Alias for single-precision floating-point Swagger data type.

objects.definition: typedef double Double;
objects.description: Alias for double-precision floating-point Swagger data type.

objects.definition: typedef std::string String;
objects.description: Alias for std::string Swagger string data type.

objects.definition: typedef char Byte;
objects.description: Alias for a byte (char) Swagger data type with format byte.

objects.definition: typedef std::vector<std::uint8_t> Binary;
objects.description: Alias representing arbitrary binary data as a vector of bytes.

objects.definition: typedef bool Bool;
objects.description: Alias for boolean Swagger data type.

objects.definition:
struct Date
{ };
objects.description: Marker type for a Swagger date (ISO date) value. No runtime data; used for schema/type metadata.

objects.definition:
struct Datetime
{ };
objects.description: Marker type for Swagger date-time values (ISO 8601). No runtime data; used for schema/type metadata.

objects.definition:
struct Password
{ };
objects.description: Marker type indicating a password string in Swagger schema. No runtime data.

objects.definition:
struct Array
{ };
objects.description: Marker type indicating an array type in Swagger schema. No runtime data; actual element type not encoded here.
Enumeration of supported URL schemes for API endpoints.
Holds global or route-level produced and consumed MIME media types.
Contact metadata for API info (name, URL, email).
License metadata for API info (name and URL).
Top-level API information (title, version, description, terms, optional contact and license).
Fluent builder to populate Schema::Info fields.
Abstract runtime descriptor for a Swagger data type, providing name, format, and validation.
Describes an operation parameter, including name, description, required flag, and associated DataType.
Represents an HTTP response specification (status code and description) for a path operation.
Fluent builder for constructing a Response object; implicitly convertible to Response.
Lightweight declaration pairing a path fragment with an HTTP method.
Represents a full route definition with path, method, description, visibility, media types, parameters, responses, and bound handler.
Container organizing Path instances by base name; provides queries, insertion, and flat iteration. Includes nested Group subtype and a Format enum.
Fluent builder for Path objects, allowing configuration of media types, parameters, responses, handler binding, and visibility.
Helper to build nested route hierarchies with a shared prefix and common parameters, delegating to a PathGroup.
Top-level REST API description object that aggregates Info, server host/base path, schemes, global media types, and declared routes.
Encapsulates Swagger UI and JSON generation/serving for a Description; allows configuring UI/API paths and custom serializer.
Nested container type within PathGroup representing a collection of Path entries for a single key, with helper to determine if all are hidden.

objects.definition:
enum class Format { Default,
                    Swagger };
objects.description: Enum inside PathGroup selecting output/iteration formatting; values are Default and Swagger.

objects.definition:
#ifdef _IS_WINDOWS
#define em_socket_t intptr_t
#else
#define em_socket_t int
#endif
objects.description: Macro-defined alias for the platform’s native socket handle integer type. On Windows it expands to intptr_t; on non-Windows it expands to int. Intended to be wide enough to store values returned by socket() or accept(). Note: this is a macro, not a typedef, so it does not create a distinct type at the C level.

No structs, enums, typedefs, classes, or other user-defined types are defined in this header. The file only contains preprocessor macros and conditional compilation directives to select libevent usage across platforms.

Fluent configuration struct for Endpoint. Holds thread count/name, TCP flags, backlog, max request/response sizes, and various timeout and logging options. Methods return Options& to allow chaining. Construction is internal (private default constructor) and typically produced via Endpoint::options() or default parameter of Endpoint::init. Some setters are templates accepting any std::chrono duration converted to milliseconds. Deprecated maxPayload maps to maxRequestSize.

HTTP server endpoint wrapper built on Pistache. Manages a Tcp::Listener, handler binding, lifecycle (bind/serve/shutdown), SSL setup, and configuration via nested Options. Provides synchronous and threaded serving and load-querying utilities.

Alias that represents a file-descriptor-like handle used by eventmeth. When _USE_LIBEVENT is defined, it is an opaque pointer to EmEvent; otherwise it is an int. Acts as the unified FD abstraction throughout the API.

Exception class in Pistache::Tcp indicating socket-related failures. It derives from std::runtime_error and forwards a C-string message to the base class. Construction requires an error message; it carries no additional state. Use it to signal errors when operating on TCP sockets. Destruction is via the base class and is noexcept. No further details are provided in this header.

Exception class in Pistache::Tcp representing server-related failures. It derives from std::runtime_error and takes a C-string error message. No additional members or behavior beyond std::runtime_error are defined.
Primary template forward declaration plus specialization mapping a size equal to sizeof(uint8_t) to the underlying integral type uint8_t. Used to deduce an underlying integer type by size.
Specialization of TypeStorage mapping a size equal to sizeof(uint16_t) to uint16_t.
Specialization of TypeStorage mapping a size equal to sizeof(uint32_t) to uint32_t.
Specialization of TypeStorage mapping a size equal to sizeof(uint64_t) to uint64_t.
Strongly-typed enum of HTTP methods. Values are generated by the HTTP_METHODS macro and include standard and WebDAV methods (e.g., Get, Post, Put, Delete, Patch, etc.).
Strongly-typed enum of HTTP status codes where each enumerator maps to its integer code (e.g., Ok=200, Not_Found=404). Values are generated by STATUS_CODES.
HTTP protocol version enumeration (HTTP/1.0 or HTTP/1.1).
Connection header control policy: Close, KeepAlive, or extension token (Ext).

objects.definition:
enum class Expectation { Continue,
                             Ext };
objects.description: Expectation header values supported: Continue or extension token (Ext).

Represents a Cache-Control directive. Some directives carry an associated delta time (e.g., MaxAge, SMaxAge, MaxStale, MinFresh) stored in a tagged-union. Provides constructors for directive-only and directive-with-delta. Users should respect which directives allow a delta.
Represents an HTTP-date (RFC 7231). Supports multiple textual formats and provides write() for formatted output and fromString() for parsing. Internally stores a system_clock::time_point.
Exception type representing an HTTP error with status code and reason message. Provides what(), code(), and reason(). Constructible from Code enum or integer code.
Template specialization enabling std::hash for Pistache::Http::Method, allowing use as keys in unordered containers.

objects.definition:
struct prototype_tag
{ };
objects.description: Marker type used to tag HTTP handler prototypes. Presence is checked via IsHttpPrototype.
Base HTTP message containing protocol version, status/code, headers, cookies, and body. Serves as common base for Request and Response.
Represents and manipulates the URI query string as a map of key/value pairs with helpers for retrieval and formatting.

objects.definition: class RequestBuilder;
objects.description: Forward declaration of an experimental RequestBuilder class. No definition provided here.
Immutable view and storage for an HTTP request, including method, resource path, parsed query parameters, client address, and timeout.
Encapsulates a one-shot or repeating response timeout tied to a Transport and Peer. Provides arm/disarm logic and invokes handler on expiry.
Chunked response writer supporting operator<< for chunked transfer and manual flushing/ending. Holds a Message, peer, buffer, transport, and Timeout.
HTTP response message; currently adds no new fields beyond Message but is parsed and sent by ResponseWriter.
Primary API for sending HTTP responses. Manages buffering, headers/cookies, content encoding, timeouts, and supports streaming or whole-body sends.
Finite-state result for parser steps: request more input (Again), proceed to next step (Next), or finished (Done).

objects.definition: using StepId = uint64_t;
objects.description: Alias for identifying parser steps with a 64-bit id. Pointer type here refers to the alias name.
Abstract parser step operating on a Message. Derived classes parse request/response line, headers, or body with a StreamCursor.
Parses the HTTP request line into a Request object.
Parses the HTTP status line into a Response object.
Parses HTTP headers into the provided Message (Request or Response).
Parses message body according to either Content-Length or chunked Transfer-Encoding. Contains a nested Chunk helper for chunked parsing.
Base class for HTTP parsers that orchestrates step execution and buffering. Aliased publicly as Pistache::Http::Parser.
Specialized parser implementation for HTTP requests. Stores a Request instance and the time the parsing started. Public alias: RequestParser.
Specialized parser implementation for HTTP responses. Stores a Response instance. Public alias: ResponseParser.
Abstract base for HTTP handlers. Receives requests and writes responses, controls parser acquisition and configurable size/time limits.
Enumeration of HTTP content/transfer encoding identifiers used by Pistache headers to represent Accept-Encoding, Content-Encoding, and Transfer-Encoding values.

Abstract base class for all HTTP header types. Provides the interface for parsing from strings or raw buffers and writing to an output stream. Implementations supply a compile-time name (and hash when SAFE_HEADER_CAST is enabled) via the NAME macro.

Traits helper to detect whether a type is a Pistache header (has static Name and derives from Header). Used by header_cast for safe downcasting. This is a template struct, not intended to be instantiated.
Represents the Allow header, listing permitted HTTP methods for a resource.
Represents the Accept header specifying acceptable media types for the response.
CORS header specifying origins allowed to access the resource.
CORS header listing allowed request headers.
CORS header listing response headers exposed to the browser.
CORS header enumerating allowed HTTP methods for cross-origin requests.
Represents the Cache-Control header holding a list of cache directives.
Represents the Connection header indicating control options like keep-alive or close.
Abstract helper header for headers carrying a single Encoding value. Base of ContentEncoding and TransferEncoding.
Represents the Accept-Encoding header with a list of encodings and their q-values, sorted by preference.
Represents the Content-Encoding header specifying the encoding applied to the payload.
Represents the Transfer-Encoding header specifying the encoding used for message transfer.
Represents the Content-Length header carrying the payload size in bytes.
Represents the Authorization header. Supports Basic and Bearer schemes with helpers to inspect and encode/decode Basic credentials.
Represents the Content-Type header holding a Mime::MediaType value.
Represents the Date header storing a FullDate timestamp.
Represents the ETag header with support for weak validators. Provides validation helpers per RFC 9110.
Represents the Expect header, commonly used with 100-continue expectations.
Represents the Host header containing the target host and optional port.
Represents the Last-Modified header carrying a FullDate timestamp for resource modification time.
Represents the Location header indicating the URL to redirect to or the location of a created resource.
Represents the Server header containing product tokens that identify the server software.
Represents the User-Agent header describing the client software.
Simple value type holding an arbitrary header name and value pair; useful for working with headers generically.
Authorization method kinds used within the Authorization header implementation.
Hash functor for case-insensitive string keys. It hashes the lowercase form of the input key and is intended for unordered_map/set keying of HTTP header names.
Binary predicate for case-insensitive equality of std::string, suitable as the key-equality comparator in unordered containers of header names.

Container managing parsed and raw HTTP headers. Provides typed access (get/tryGet/has), insertion (add/addRaw), removal, listing, and case-insensitive lookup via custom hash/equality. Owns maps keyed by header name to Header objects and Raw values.

Singleton registry for HTTP header types. Allows registering header classes, querying registration, listing names, and constructing Header instances by name using stored factory functions. Copying disabled.

Nested struct inside Pistache::Tcp::Listener that captures CPU/load metrics: an overall global value, per-worker values, raw resource-usage snapshots, and the timestamp of the sample. Used as the payload for requestLoad(). Specific semantics of the fields (units, aggregation) are not documented here and must be inferred from surrounding code.

TCP listener class responsible for binding to an address/port, accepting connections, and dispatching peers to worker transports/reactor. Supports configuration (workers, options, backlog, logger), SSL setup, and load reporting. Lifecycle: construct, init, bind, run/runThreaded, shutdown. Ownership: manages sockets, poller, worker/reactor resources, and SSL context.

objects.definition: using TransportFactory = std::function<std::shared_ptr<Transport>()>;
objects.description: Type alias for a factory functor that creates shared Transport instances for dispatching peers. Set via setTransportFactory; if not set, defaultTransportFactory() is used. Note: this is a type alias only; actual Transport type is forward-declared here.

objects.definition:
#ifndef PISTACHE_STRING_LOGGER_T
#define PISTACHE_STRING_LOGGER_T \
    std::shared_ptr<::Pistache::Log::StringLogger>
#endif
objects.description: Macro alias for the type std::shared_ptr<::Pistache::Log::StringLogger>. This header does not define StringLogger itself; it is pulled in from <pistache/string_logger.h>. The macro provides a convenient name for a shared pointer to a Pistache string logger.

objects.definition: typedef char cacheline_pad_t[CachelineSize];
objects.description: Fixed-size character array used as cacheline padding (64 bytes) to avoid false sharing in concurrent data structures.
Enumeration of top-level MIME types (e.g., text, image, audio, video, application, message, multipart) plus Star and None. Used as the primary media type component.
Enumeration of MIME subtypes (e.g., plain, html, json, png) plus Star and special values Vendor, Ext, and None. Represents the second component of a MIME type.
Enumeration of MIME structured syntax suffixes (e.g., +json, +xml), with special values None and Ext.

Quality value wrapper for MIME quality parameters (q-values). Stores an integer in [0,100] representing 0.00–1.00 as percent. Provides construction from integer (throws if out of range) and from float via fromFloat, accessors, conversion operator, and string formatting. Comparison operator== is also defined in this header.

Type-safe representation of a MIME media type. Holds top-level type, subtype, optional suffix, raw serialized form with substring indices, parameters map, and optional quality value. Provides constructors from components or raw string, parsing support, accessors, and serialization. Equality and inequality operators are defined in this header. Nested helper struct Index is private and thus not part of public API.

objects.definition:
enum Parse { DoParse,
                     DontParse };
objects.description: Helper enum controlling whether MediaType(string) constructor parses the input immediately or stores it raw.
Typedef alias for an unsigned 64-bit integer provided by <cstdint>. This is a standard library typedef, not defined in this header, and therefore should be ignored per instructions.

RAII wrapper for getaddrinfo(). Stores the result list and frees it with freeaddrinfo in the destructor. Non-copyable. Use invoke() to populate and get_info_ptr() to read the const addrinfo list pointer.
Small value-class representing a TCP/UDP port. Construct from integer or string, convertible to uint16_t. Provides helpers for reserved/used checks and string conversion.

Abstraction over IPv4/IPv6 socket addresses backed by sockaddr_storage. Provides constructors for v4 and v6 literals, helpers for any/loopback, conversions to network types, and access to family/port and underlying sockaddr. Ipv4/Ipv6 are aliases of IP.
Utility to parse address strings into host and port components with metadata about presence of colon, numeric port, and detected family. Stores parsed fields.

Represents a network or UNIX-domain address including host/IP, port, address family, and optional HTTP scheme/page. Wraps an IP and Port, provides multiple constructors (string, C-string, IP+Port), factory with default port and scheme, and conversion/accessors. Supports AF_INET, AF_INET6, and AF_UNIX.
Exception type for networking errors, derived from std::runtime_error. Provides constructors from C-string or std::string and a helper to create a system error.
Specialization of Size functor for C strings; returns strlen(s).
Size functor specialization for uint8_t; returns number of base-10 digits.
Size functor specialization for int8_t; returns number of base-10 digits.
Size functor specialization for uint16_t; returns number of base-10 digits.
Size functor specialization for int16_t; returns number of base-10 digits.
Size functor specialization for uint32_t; returns number of base-10 digits.
Size functor specialization for int32_t; returns number of base-10 digits.
Size functor specialization for uint64_t; returns number of base-10 digits.
Size functor specialization for int64_t; returns number of base-10 digits.
Size functor specialization for bool; returns 1.
Size functor specialization for char; returns 1.
Enumeration of HTTP schemes used by Address to annotate addresses with HTTP/HTTPS or unspecified.
Affinity bitset helper with capacity for up to 1024 CPUs. Provides methods to set/unset single CPUs or ranges, query membership and count, and optionally convert to a POSIX cpu_set_t when available.

objects.definition:
enum class Mode { Level,
                          Edge };
objects.description: Polling mode selector for Epoll-like mechanisms: level-triggered or edge-triggered.
Bitflag enumeration specifying I/O events of interest for polling: read, write, hangup, shutdown. Operators are enabled via DECLARE_FLAGS_OPERATORS elsewhere.
Lightweight wrapper for an implementation-dependent tagging value associated with a polled FD. Provides accessors to raw value and to actual numeric FD value across backends.
Represents a single polled event: a tag identifying the source and a set of NotifyOn flags indicating what occurred.

Abstraction over the OS polling mechanism (epoll or libevent-backed equivalent). Manages registration of FDs with event interests, supports one-shot and rearm semantics, and provides a thread-safety mutex for registration/unregistration coordination.
Lightweight event notification FD wrapper that can be bound to a Polling::Epoll instance. Provides notify and read/tryRead operations and tracks its binding/tag.

objects.definition: class Transport;
objects.description: Forward declaration of a TCP transport class within Pistache::Tcp. Only a declaration is present; no members are defined in this header, so details and lifecycle are unknown.

Represents a TCP peer (remote endpoint) managed by Pistache::Tcp. Provides access to its address, file descriptor, optional SSL pointer, hostname caching, user-attached data map, async send, and idle state. Constructed via static factory methods returning std::shared_ptr. It keeps a back-pointer to Transport for I/O operations. Destruction and low-level behavior are defined elsewhere. Note: Address, Fd, RawBuffer, PST_SSIZE_T, em_socket_t, PS_FD_EMPTY originate from other headers; specifics not defined here.
Clock identifier type used with PST_CLOCK_GETTIME. It is referenced here but defined in pistache/winornix.h, not in this header. Definition unavailable in this file.
Timespec-like structure holding seconds/nanoseconds for time retrieval on Windows shims. Forward-referenced here via pointer but its full definition is in pistache/winornix.h, not this header.

Opaque socket-handle type referenced from <pistache/em_socket_t.h>. It is not defined in this header; only used as a parameter type to PST_FCNTL. Details such as representation and lifetime are unknown from this file.

No custom structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only declares functions (pist_pread, pist_open overloads) and includes win/nix portability macros and standard types. Types like PST_SSIZE_T and PST_FILE_MODE_T are referenced but not defined here.

Windows-compatible interface address record mimicking Linux getifaddrs struct. It forms a linked list of network interfaces with name, flags, primary address, netmask, and either broadcast or destination address via the ifa_ifu union. Access macros pist_ifa_broadaddr and pist_ifa_dstaddr map to the union members. Intended to be produced by PST_GETIFADDRS and freed by PST_FREEIFADDRS. Lifetime is managed by the caller; free the entire list using PST_FREEIFADDRS. Details about sockaddr variants depend on the system headers and are not defined here.

No custom types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. It only defines preprocessor macros PIST_Q and PIST_QUOTE for stringizing macro arguments, guarded by an include guard.
Windows-side replacement for the POSIX struct rusage, holding user and system CPU time via two struct timeval fields. Present only when _IS_WINDOWS is defined.

objects.definition: typedef struct fd_set fd_set;
objects.description: Forward declaration typedef for the Winsock/FD set structure used with select(). Only a typedef to an incomplete struct is provided here; the actual definition lives in platform headers. Use as an opaque set of sockets for pist_sock_select and related calls.
Poll descriptor entry used by pist_sock_poll. Holds an em_socket_t and event masks to request and report readiness/errors. The layout mirrors POSIX struct pollfd but uses em_socket_t for fd.
No custom types are defined in this header. It only declares the function pist_strerror_r and includes standard/platform headers. There are no structs, enums, typedefs, or classes introduced here.

Logging stream facade class providing five std::ostream members (debug, info, warning, error, alert) intended to route stream-style output to the logging backend. Only the class declaration is present here; member behavior and routing are not defined in this header. A default constructor is declared but not defined here.

PST_SSIZE_T is referenced as the return type of ps_sendfile, but it is not defined in this header. It is presumably a typedef defined in pistache/emosandlibevdefs.h (or related headers) that represents a signed size type compatible with ssize_t across platforms. Since this header does not define it, we cannot document its exact definition here.

em_socket_t is referenced as the socket descriptor type for the out_fd parameter of ps_sendfile, but it is not defined in this header. It is likely a platform-abstracted socket handle typedef defined in pistache/em_socket_t.h. No definition is present here.

No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only declares C-linkage functions (ps_strlcpy, ps_strlcat, ps_strncpy_s) and preprocessor macros. Therefore, there are no custom data types to document.
A container of ready file-descriptor events produced by the poller. Provides iteration over entries with helpers to test readability, writability, and hangup state and fetch the associated tag.
An individual ready event, privately derived from Polling::Event, exposing convenience inspectors and the stored tag.
Central AIO reactor that registers, modifies, removes FDs and dispatches readiness events to handlers. Internally delegates to platform-specific Impl via ExecutionContext.
Opaque token identifying a registration context within the Reactor; used to associate handlers and FD registrations.
Abstract factory for creating a Reactor::Impl appropriate to the execution model (sync/async).
ExecutionContext that constructs a synchronous single-threaded Reactor implementation.
ExecutionContext that constructs an asynchronous Reactor implementation using a thread pool. Holds thread count and optional naming prefix.
Base class for AIO event handlers. Must implement onReady and poller registration hooks. Holds back-reference to the Reactor, execution context info, and its registration key.
Lightweight execution context for a Handler capturing the thread id where the handler runs.
Holds a named parameter (path param or splat) extracted by the router with helpers to cast its string value to a specific type.
Routing entry abstractions: defines handler, middleware and disconnect handler function signatures, plus routing result/status enums. Holds a Handler instance.
Node of a tree-based router storing child segments (fixed, param, optional, splat) and an associated Route. Provides add/remove/find and resource sanitization.
HTTP REST router that manages method-specific SegmentTreeNode collections, route registration APIs, middleware, custom and not-found handlers, and dispatches requests.
Http::Handler implementation that delegates request and disconnection handling to a Rest::Router (immutable or shared).
Augmented Http::Request that exposes route parameters and splats parsed by the router.

Custom deleter functor for use with unique_ptr<void> that frees an OpenSSL SSL_CTX and invokes EVP_cleanup (when PISTACHE_USE_SSL is defined). Intended to manage the lifetime of an SSL context via RAII. If PISTACHE_USE_SSL is not defined, operator() is a no-op.
Custom deleter functor for use with unique_ptr<void> that frees an OpenSSL BIO (when PISTACHE_USE_SSL is defined). Provides RAII cleanup for BIO resources; no-op when PISTACHE_USE_SSL is not defined.

objects.definition: using SSLCtxPtr = std::unique_ptr<void, SSLCtxDeleter>;
objects.description: Type alias for a unique_ptr managing a raw SSL context pointer stored as void*, using SSLCtxDeleter for cleanup. Call get() and reinterpret to SSL_CTX* when PISTACHE_USE_SSL is enabled.

objects.definition: using SSLBioPtr = std::unique_ptr<void, SSLBioDeleter>;
objects.description: Type alias for a unique_ptr managing a raw BIO pointer stored as void*, using SSLBioDeleter for cleanup. Call get() and reinterpret to BIO* when PISTACHE_USE_SSL is enabled.

Template stream buffer wrapper over std::basic_streambuf providing helper accessors to the get area, position tracking, a safe reset, and a lookahead (snext). On MinGW builds it explicitly sets the locale to "C" to avoid a destruction-time crash. Used as the base for other Pistache stream buffers.
Lightweight StreamBuf that exposes a read-only get area over an existing contiguous memory range without owning it. Useful to parse in-place buffers.

Owning, dynamically growable read buffer backed by std::vector. Supports feeding more bytes up to a maximum size while preserving the current read offset; can reset to empty. Useful for incremental parsing with bounded memory.
Small value-type wrapper for a byte sequence plus an explicit logical length. Provides copying from an offset and read-only accessors. Storage is in a std::string; length_ may be <= data_.size().

Represents a memory-light reference to a file payload, opening a file by name and exposing its file descriptor and size. Manages filename, fd, and size; detailed lifetime/ownership semantics of fd are not shown here.

Writable stream buffer that grows dynamically up to a maximum size and can expose its accumulated data as a RawBuffer. Overrides overflow() to append, supports clear() and move semantics; copying is disabled.

Cursor/reader over a StreamBuf<char> providing position management, lookahead, tokenization (Token snapshot with text extraction), and RAII rollback (Revert). Useful for parsers to navigate the input and optionally revert state.

objects.definition:
enum class CaseSensitivity { Sensitive,
                             Insensitive };
objects.description: Enumeration to control case sensitivity when matching text in the stream parsing helpers.
Strongly-typed logging severity enumeration for the Pistache::Log subsystem. Values range from trace to fatal. Used to classify and filter log messages.

Abstract base class for string-based loggers in Pistache. Provides a virtual interface to log messages at a given Level and to query if a level is enabled. Intended to be subclassed by concrete logger implementations. Ownership/lifetime is managed by user; destructor is virtual.

Concrete logger that writes string messages to a std::ostream (defaults to std::cerr). Maintains a minimum enabled Level threshold and forwards messages meeting that threshold to the configured stream. Does not own the provided std::ostream pointer; caller must ensure its lifetime exceeds that of the logger.

Scoped enum of TCP socket option flags used within Pistache::Tcp. Values are bit flags suitable for combination via DECLARE_FLAGS_OPERATORS(Options). Abstract base class for TCP connection handlers in Pistache::Tcp. A pool class that manages reusable timer file descriptors to minimize system calls. Provides methods to pick and release timers (as shared_ptr to nested Entry objects). Construction accepts an initial pool size. Details of how timers are created/managed are implemented elsewhere.

Represents a single timer resource within TimerPool. Holds a file descriptor and registration state, can be initialized, armed for a duration, disarmed, and registered with a reactor. Internal state is tracked lock-free via an atomic state field. Implementation details (fd creation, arming/disarming mechanics) are not present in this header.

TCP transport layer handler for Pistache. Manages peers, timers, and asynchronous writes over file descriptors. Implements Aio::Handler to integrate with reactor/poller. Provides queuing for writes, timer arming/disarming, and load reporting. Constructors require a Tcp::Handler shared_ptr. Destruction/ownership semantics beyond RAII are not documented here.

A small, comparable, hashable type-identifier class. For each unique template parameter T, TypeId::of<T>() returns a distinct TypeId value derived from the address of a TU-local static. It converts to size_t for hashing and comparison and provides ==, !=, and < operators. Internally stores an opaque pointer-sized token (void const*).
std::hash specialization enabling Pistache::TypeId to be used as a key in unordered associative containers. Hash value is the size_t conversion of the TypeId.

functions.description: Formats the given arguments using the provided std::format-style format string and writes the result to the output stream, returning the same stream. This is a compatibility helper placed in namespace date for environments using std::chrono, providing a to_stream overload that leverages std::format. Typical usage: pass a valid std::basic_ostream (e.g., std::cout), a compile-time-checked std::format_string and corresponding arguments; the function forwards to std::format(fmt, args...) and inserts the result into the stream. requirements: Underlying iterator must not be the container's end() when incrementing; incrementing end() is undefined.
The underlying iterator must be valid; it must come from a live Map instance that outlives the adapter.
The Map must be a map-like type exposing key_type, mapped_type, and const_iterator and whose value_type supports .second.

functions.name: Pistache::FlatMapIteratorAdapter::operator*
functions.description: Dereference operator for the FlatMapIteratorAdapter. Returns a const reference to the mapped value (it->second) at the current iterator position. This flattens a map-like iterator of pair<const Key, Value> into direct access to Value.
requirements: The underlying iterator must be dereferenceable (not equal to end()).
The underlying iterator must be valid and not invalidated by modifications to the Map.
Returned reference remains valid only as long as the underlying Map element remains valid (i.e., until iterator invalidation or element removal).

functions.name: Pistache::FlatMapIteratorAdapter::operator==
functions.description: Equality comparison for two FlatMapIteratorAdapter instances. Compares equality of the underlying Map::const_iterator values.
requirements: Both adapters must be instantiated with the same Map type.
Both adapters should originate from the same Map instance or from containers where comparing iterators is well-defined; comparing iterators from different containers is undefined.
The underlying iterators must be valid (not invalidated).

functions.name: Pistache::FlatMapIteratorAdapter::operator!=
functions.description: Inequality comparison for two FlatMapIteratorAdapter instances. Returns the negation of operator== on the underlying iterators.
requirements: Both adapters must be instantiated with the same Map type.
Both adapters should originate from the same Map instance or from containers where comparing iterators is well-defined; comparing iterators from different containers is undefined.
The underlying iterators must be valid (not invalidated).

functions.name: Pistache::makeFlatMapIterator
functions.signature:
template <typename Map>
Pistache::FlatMapIteratorAdapter<Map> Pistache::makeFlatMapIterator(const Map&, typename Map::const_iterator it)
functions.description: Factory helper that constructs a FlatMapIteratorAdapter from a Map::const_iterator. Use to adapt a map-like const_iterator so that dereferencing yields the mapped value directly.
requirements: The Map template parameter must define key_type, mapped_type, and const_iterator consistent with a map-like container (value_type with .second).
Argument it must be a valid const_iterator into a Map instance of the same type; it must be dereferenceable before calling operator* on the returned adapter.
The Map instance from which it originates must outlive the returned adapter; any modifications that invalidate iterators will invalidate the adapter.
Do not dereference the returned adapter when it equals the end iterator; behavior is undefined.

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::setSocketOptions
functions.description: Configure socket options on the given socket descriptor. Intended to apply Pistache TCP Options flags to an already-created socket.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open socket file descriptor
options should contain a valid combination of Pistache::Tcp::Options flags
Caller must handle any errors/signals raised by underlying OS setsockopt calls (unknown in this header)

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::Listener
functions.description: Default-construct a TCP Listener. The instance is not bound or running until init/bind/run are called.
requirements: No specific requirements at construction time
Before accepting connections, caller should initialize and bind the listener (see init(), bind(), run())

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::Listener
functions.description: Construct a TCP Listener bound to a specific address object (not yet listening). Use bind()/run() to start accepting connections.
requirements: address must contain a valid IP/port or service that can later be bound
Before accepting connections, caller should call bind() and then run()

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::~Listener
functions.description: Destructor for the TCP Listener. Cleans up resources (e.g., sockets, threads, reactor) associated with the listener.
requirements: If runThreaded() was used, ensure shutdown() has been called or that destruction occurs when no threads are actively using the listener (exact behavior unknown from header)

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::init
functions.signature: void Pistache::Tcp::Listener::init(size_t workers, Flags<Options> options = Flags<Options>(Options::None), const std::string& workersName = "", int backlog = Const::MaxBacklog, PISTACHE_STRING_LOGGER_T logger = PISTACHE_NULL_STRING_LOGGER);
functions.description: Initialize the listener’s worker pool, options, backlog, and optional logger before binding/running. Typically called once per Listener instance.
requirements: workers must be a non-zero size_t (exact minimum not specified; zero is likely invalid by convention)
options must be a valid combination of Pistache::Tcp::Options flags
backlog must be a non-negative integer and typically within OS limits (Const::MaxBacklog by default)
Should be called before bind() and run()
If provided, logger must remain valid for the duration it is used by the listener (exact ownership semantics unknown)

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::setTransportFactory
functions.description: Install a factory to create Transport instances used for handling accepted connections.
requirements: factory must be a callable that returns std::shared_ptr<Pistache::Tcp::Transport>
Must be set before starting the listener with run()/runThreaded() to ensure it is used for new connections

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::setHandler
functions.description: Attach a request/connection handler used by the listener/transport to process incoming data.
requirements: handler must be a non-null shared_ptr to a valid Handler instance
Must be called before run()/runThreaded() so that connections have a handler to dispatch to
Handler should be thread-safe if multiple workers are configured (thread-safety details unknown in this header)

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::bind
functions.description: Bind the listener to its configured address (e.g., set in constructor or via init/address setters).
requirements: The listener must have a valid address configured prior to calling bind()
Socket options and backlog should be configured via init() before binding
May only be called when the listener is not already bound (exact rebind behavior unknown)

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::bind
functions.description: Bind the listener to the specified address and prepare to accept connections.
requirements: address must contain a valid IP/port (or hostname/service) that the process has permission to bind to
init() should be called before bind() to configure options and backlog
May only be called when the listener is not already bound (exact rebind behavior unknown)

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::isBound
functions.description: Query whether the listener has successfully bound its listening socket.

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::getPort
functions.description: Return the port number on which the listener is bound. Useful when binding to port 0 to discover the assigned ephemeral port.
requirements: Should only be called after a successful bind(); otherwise the returned value may be undefined (details not specified)

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::run
functions.description: Run the listener’s accept loop and worker processing in the current thread until shutdown() is invoked.
requirements: bind() must have been successfully called before run()
A handler should be set via setHandler() before calling run()
Should not be used concurrently with runThreaded() on the same instance

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::runThreaded
functions.description: Start the listener’s accept loop and worker processing on a background thread, returning immediately.
requirements: bind() must have been successfully called before runThreaded()
A handler should be set via setHandler() before calling runThreaded()
Should not be called multiple times or together with run() on the same instance (exact enforcement unknown)
Caller is responsible for later invoking shutdown() and joining/allowing threads to terminate (exact lifecycle details unknown)

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::shutdown
functions.description: Stop the listener, signal the accept loop and workers to terminate, and close associated resources.
requirements: May be called safely after run() or runThreaded() to stop the listener (exact idempotency unknown)

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::requestLoad
functions.description: Asynchronously request current load metrics from the listener/workers, optionally using a prior Load snapshot to compute deltas or trends.
requirements: old should be a previously captured Load sample from this listener instance (can be default/empty if no prior sample)
Caller must handle the returned Async::Promise appropriately (e.g., set continuations, wait) according to Pistache Async semantics

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::options
functions.description: Return the current TCP listener options.

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::address
functions.description: Return the configured listening address for this listener.

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::pinWorker
functions.signature: void Pistache::Tcp::Listener::pinWorker(size_t worker, const CpuSet& set);
functions.description: Pin or affinitize a worker thread to the specified CPU set, controlling where the worker executes.
requirements: worker index must refer to an existing worker in the pool (0 <= worker < configured workers count)
set must describe a valid CpuSet mask on the host system
Should be called after init() and before or during run(), depending on implementation (exact timing not specified)

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::setupSSL
functions.signature: void Pistache::Tcp::Listener::setupSSL(const std::string& cert_path, const std::string& key_path, bool use_compression, int (*cb_password)(char*, int, int, void*), std::chrono::milliseconds sslHandshakeTimeout = Const::DefaultSSLHandshakeTimeout);
functions.description: Configure TLS/SSL for the listener with certificate and key files, optional password callback for encrypted keys, optional compression, and a handshake timeout.
requirements: The library/build must be compiled with PISTACHE_USE_SSL enabled
cert_path must point to a readable X.509 certificate file
key_path must point to the corresponding readable private key file
cb_password, if the key is encrypted, must be a valid function pointer with signature int(char*, int, int, void*) or can be nullptr if not needed
sslHandshakeTimeout must be a non-negative duration
Must be called before binding/accepting SSL connections (i.e., before run()/runThreaded())

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::setupSSLAuth
functions.signature: void Pistache::Tcp::Listener::setupSSLAuth(const std::string& ca_file, const std::string& ca_path, int (*cb)(int, void*));
functions.description: Enable and configure SSL/TLS client authentication (mTLS) using CA certificates and a verification callback.
requirements: The library/build must be compiled with PISTACHE_USE_SSL enabled
ca_file and/or ca_path must refer to readable CA certificate bundle/file locations
cb must be a valid verification callback with signature int(int, void*) compatible with the SSL library expectations
Must be called after setupSSL() and before accepting SSL connections

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Listener::getAllPeer
functions.description: Return a snapshot list of all current connected peers managed by the listener.
requirements: May return an empty vector if no peers are connected
Thread-safety of concurrent access is unspecified in this header

functions.name: Pistache::Mailbox<T>::get
functions.signature: template <typename T> const T* Pistache::Mailbox<T>::get() const
functions.description: Returns the current pointer stored in the mailbox. Throws std::runtime_error if the mailbox is empty. Typical use is to read the last posted pointer value in an MPSC-style pattern.
requirements: The mailbox must not be empty; otherwise this function throws std::runtime_error("Can not retrieve mail from empty mailbox").
Return value is the raw pointer previously posted; ownership and lifetime are managed by the caller (unknown from header).
Thread-safety: internally uses an atomic pointer; concurrent posts are safe by lock-free CAS.

functions.name: Pistache::Mailbox<T>::post
functions.description: Atomically replaces the stored pointer with newData and returns the previous pointer. Useful for MPSC communication where producers update a single slot.
requirements: newData may be null; no explicit restriction is stated.
Caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of both the previous pointer (returned) and the new pointer (posted); ownership semantics are not defined in the header.
Safe for concurrent producers; uses atomic compare_exchange_weak in a loop.

functions.name: Pistache::Mailbox<T>::clear
functions.description: Atomically clears the mailbox (sets it to nullptr) and returns the previously stored pointer.
requirements: Caller is responsible for disposing of the returned pointer, if any; ownership semantics are not defined in the header.

functions.name: Pistache::Mailbox<T>::isEmpty
functions.description: Checks whether the mailbox currently holds a null pointer.

functions.name: Pistache::PollableMailbox<T>::isBound
functions.description: Returns true if the mailbox has been bound to a poller and has a valid event file descriptor.

functions.name: Pistache::PollableMailbox<T>::bind
functions.description: Creates an eventfd and registers it with the provided poller to make the mailbox pollable for read events. Returns the associated polling tag.
requirements: Must not already be bound; otherwise throws std::runtime_error("The mailbox has already been bound").
poller must be a valid Pistache::Polling::Epoll instance capable of addFd.
On success, the eventfd is added with NotifyOn::Read; caller should later unbind/close via unbind().

functions.name: Pistache::PollableMailbox<T>::post
functions.description: Posts a new pointer to the mailbox (as in Mailbox::post) and, if bound, signals the eventfd to wake any poller waiting for read readiness. Returns the previous pointer.
requirements: Same ownership requirements as Mailbox::post (caller manages previous and new pointers).
If bound, WRITE_EFD must succeed; errors propagate via TRY macro semantics (unknown exact behavior).

functions.name: Pistache::PollableMailbox<T>::clear
functions.description: Clears the mailbox (as in Mailbox::clear) and, if bound, drains the eventfd by reading until EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK to reset readiness. Returns the previously stored pointer.
requirements: Caller manages lifetime of the returned pointer.
If bound, eventfd reads are attempted until non-blocking would occur; unexpected read errors are noted but not fully handled in this header (TODO).

functions.name: Pistache::PollableMailbox<T>::tag
functions.description: Returns the polling tag associated with the bound mailbox's eventfd.
requirements: Mailbox must be bound; otherwise throws std::runtime_error("Can not retrieve tag of an unbound mailbox").

functions.name: Pistache::PollableMailbox<T>::unbind
functions.description: Removes the mailbox's eventfd from the poller and closes it, making the mailbox non-pollable.
requirements: Mailbox must be bound; otherwise throws std::runtime_error("The mailbox is not bound").
poller must be the same (or compatible) Epoll instance used to bind so removeFd operates on the correct fd.

functions.name: Pistache::Queue<T>::push
functions.signature: template <typename T> template <typename U> void Pistache::Queue<T>::push(U&& u)
functions.description: Enqueues a new element by constructing a Queue<T>::Entry holding a T built from u and appending it to the MPSC queue. Wait-free for producers.
requirements: U must be constructible into T (T must be constructible from std::forward<U>(u)).
Memory allocation for a new Entry must succeed.
Safe for multiple producers; single consumer expected by design.

functions.name: Pistache::Queue<T>::pop
functions.description: Single-consumer dequeue operation. Returns a pointer to an Entry containing a moved value of type T if available, or nullptr if the queue is empty. The returned Entry holds T in its internal storage.
requirements: Single-consumer usage is assumed; concurrent pops are not supported.
Caller takes ownership of the returned Entry and is responsible for calling std::destroy_at(&entry->data()) and deleting the Entry to avoid leaks (inferred from implementation).

functions.name: Pistache::Queue<T>::empty
functions.description: Returns true if the queue appears empty (head and tail are the same sentinel).
requirements: Due to concurrency, emptiness is a moment-in-time observation and may change immediately after the call.

functions.name: Pistache::Queue<T>::popSafe
functions.description: Convenience wrapper around pop() that returns a unique_ptr<T> to a moved-out value if available. It destroys the Entry and its contained T before returning.
requirements: Single-consumer usage is assumed.
Returned unique_ptr<T> is null if the queue was empty.

functions.name: Pistache::PollableQueue<T>::isBound
functions.description: Returns true if the queue has been bound to a poller and has a valid eventfd.

functions.name: Pistache::PollableQueue<T>::bind
functions.description: Creates an eventfd and registers it with the poller so push/pop activity can be polled for read readiness. Returns the polling tag.
requirements: Must not already be bound; otherwise throws std::runtime_error("The queue has already been bound").
poller must be a valid Pistache::Polling::Epoll instance.
On success, the fd is added with NotifyOn::Read; caller should later unbind().

functions.name: Pistache::PollableQueue<T>::unbind
functions.description: Removes the queue's eventfd from the poller and closes it. Unlike PollableMailbox::unbind, this method is tolerant of being called on an unbound queue; it logs a warning and returns.
requirements: If bound, poller must be valid to removeFd the eventfd.
Safe to call even if not bound; no exception is thrown.

functions.name: Pistache::PollableQueue<T>::push
functions.signature: template <typename T> template <class U> void Pistache::PollableQueue<T>::push(U&& u)
functions.description: Enqueues a new element (as in Queue::push) and, if bound, signals the eventfd to wake the poller.
requirements: U must be constructible into T.
If bound, WRITE_EFD must succeed; errors propagate via TRY macro semantics (unknown exact behavior).
Multiple producers supported; single consumer expected.

functions.name: Pistache::PollableQueue<T>::pop
functions.description: Dequeues one element (as in Queue::pop) and attempts to drain/adjust the eventfd to reflect the consumption. Returns nullptr if no element is available.
requirements: Single-consumer usage is assumed; concurrent pops are not supported.
Caller owns the returned Entry and must destroy its T (std::destroy_at(&entry->data())) and delete the Entry to avoid leaks (inferred from implementation).
If bound, function may perform non-blocking reads on the eventfd; unexpected errors are logged but not fully handled.

functions.name: Pistache::PollableQueue<T>::tag
functions.description: Returns the polling tag associated with the queue's eventfd.
requirements: Queue must be bound; otherwise throws std::runtime_error("Can not retrieve tag of an unbound mailbox").

functions.name: Pistache::MPMCQueue<T, Size>::enqueue
functions.signature: template <typename T, size_t Size> template <typename U> bool Pistache::MPMCQueue<T, Size>::enqueue(U&& data)
functions.description: Attempts to enqueue data into the bounded multi-producer multi-consumer queue. Returns true on success, false if the queue is full.
requirements: Template parameter Size must be a power of two and >= 2 (enforced by static_assert at class level).
U must be assignable/movable into T (T must be constructible/assignable from U).
May be called concurrently by multiple producers.

functions.name: Pistache::MPMCQueue<T, Size>::dequeue
functions.signature: template <typename T, size_t Size> bool Pistache::MPMCQueue<T, Size>::dequeue(T& data)
functions.description: Attempts to dequeue the next item into data. Returns true on success, false if the queue is empty.
requirements: data is an lvalue reference that will receive a copy/move of the dequeued T.
May be called concurrently by multiple consumers.

functions.name: Pistache::Http::Mime::Q::Q
functions.description: Constructs a MIME quality value (q) wrapper from an integer in the 0..100 range (representing 0.00..1.00 scaled by 100). Throws std::runtime_error if out of range. Use to attach or compare HTTP Accept-* quality weights.

functions.name: Pistache::Http::Mime::Q::fromFloat
functions.description: Factory that builds a Q from a floating-point quality value by rounding f*100 to the nearest integer and constructing Q with that integer. Intended for HTTP quality weights in [0.0, 1.0].
requirements: Input f should be within [0.0, 1.0] to avoid triggering the Q constructor’s range check (values producing >100 after rounding will throw via the constructor).
Rounding is applied (std::round) before conversion to the integer scale.

functions.name: Pistache::Http::Mime::Q::value
functions.description: Returns the stored scaled quality value (0..100). Use when you need the raw integer representation of the quality factor.

functions.name: Pistache::Http::Mime::Q::operator Type
functions.description: Implicit conversion operator to the underlying integer quality value (0..100). Enables using Q in integer contexts or comparisons.

functions.name: Pistache::Http::Mime::Q::toString
functions.description: Returns a string representation of the quality value. Exact format is not specified here; typically expected as a decimal between 0 and 1 with up to 2 fractional digits or an integer percentage representation. Details unknown due to missing implementation.

functions.name: Pistache::Http::Mime::MediaType::fromRaw

functions.name: Pistache::Http::Mime::MediaType::fromString

functions.name: Pistache::Http::Mime::MediaType::fromFile

functions.name: Pistache::Http::Mime::operator!=

functions.name: Pistache::Meta::Hash::fnv1a
functions.signature: inline constexpr uint64_t Pistache::Meta::Hash::fnv1a(const char* const str, const uint64_t value = val64) noexcept
functions.description: Computes a 64-bit FNV-1a hash over a null-terminated C-string. Implemented as a constexpr, tail-recursive routine that starts from the provided initial value (defaulting to the canonical 64-bit FNV-1a offset basis val64) and iteratively mixes each character using the FNV prime. Suitable for compile-time hashing of string literals as well as runtime hashing. Terminates when the '\0' character is reached. Note: as written, the per-byte mix uses the char value as seen by the implementation (no explicit unsigned cast).
requirements: str must be a non-null pointer to a valid, readable, null-terminated character sequence.
The memory pointed to by str must remain valid for the duration of the call and include a '\0' terminator.
If value is provided, it is used as the initial hash; otherwise the function defaults to Pistache::Meta::Hash::val64 (the 64-bit FNV-1a offset basis).
The function is noexcept; callers must not rely on exceptions being thrown for error reporting.
Safe to use in constant-evaluation contexts (constexpr) when str and value are usable in such contexts.

functions.name: Pistache::AddrInfo::invoke
functions.signature: int Pistache::AddrInfo::invoke(const char* node, const char* service, const struct addrinfo* hints)
