requirements: Caller must handle the possibility of PS_FD_EMPTY being returned.

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Peer::actualFd
functions.description: Returns the underlying OS/socket integer for the peer, or -1 if unavailable. Useful when an emulation or wrapper Fd is used.
requirements: Caller must handle the possibility of -1 being returned to indicate no valid underlying descriptor.

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Peer::closeFd
functions.description: Closes the peer's underlying file descriptor, rendering the peer no longer usable for I/O.
requirements: After calling closeFd, subsequent I/O (e.g., send) may fail or be invalid; callers should cease using the socket-dependent operations.
Safe to call only when no concurrent send/receive is in flight; thread-safety and synchronization are the caller’s responsibility.

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Peer::ssl
functions.description: Returns the raw SSL handle pointer associated with the peer, or nullptr if none. When SSL is enabled, this is typically an OpenSSL SSL*.
requirements: Caller must cast the void* to the appropriate SSL type if needed.
Pointer validity and lifetime are tied to the Peer; do not use after the Peer is destroyed.

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Peer::putData
functions.description: Associates arbitrary user data with the peer under a string key. Overwrites any existing entry with the same key.
requirements: name should uniquely identify the data slot for this peer.
data may be nullptr if used as a sentinel; behavior with nullptr is not explicitly documented.
Ownership of data is via shared_ptr; ensure correct type erasure and casting discipline when retrieving.

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Peer::getData
functions.description: Retrieves the user data associated with the given key, potentially throwing or asserting if missing depending on implementation (behavior not documented here). Use tryGetData for a non-throwing lookup.
requirements: name must correspond to an existing entry; behavior is unknown if the key is absent.
Returned shared_ptr may be empty if stored as such.

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Peer::tryGetData
functions.description: Attempts to retrieve user data for the given key; returns an empty shared_ptr if not found.
requirements: None beyond providing a key string. Caller should handle an empty result indicating no data for the key.

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Peer::send
functions.description: Asynchronously sends the contents of buffer to the peer, optionally using OS-dependent flags. Resolves the promise with the number of bytes written or an error according to the Async/Promise contract.
requirements: buffer must reference valid memory for the duration of the send; RawBuffer semantics determine exact lifetime requirements (not specified here).
flags must be valid for the underlying send(2)-like operation on the platform.
The peer must have a valid, open socket; calling after closeFd or on PS_FD_EMPTY may fail.
Caller should observe and handle promise resolution/rejection to detect partial writes or errors.

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::Peer::getID
functions.description: Returns this peer's unique identifier within the process. Useful for correlating logs or tracking connections.
requirements: None; the returned value is read-only and stable for the lifetime of the Peer.

functions.name: Pistache::Tcp::operator<<
functions.description: Stream insertion operator to print a human-readable representation of a Peer to an output stream (e.g., for logging/debugging).
requirements: os must be a valid output stream.
peer must be a valid object. The exact format of the output is not documented.

functions.name: PS_LogWoBreak
functions.signature: extern int PS_LogWoBreak(int pri, const char *p, const char *f, int l, const char *m = 0);
functions.description: Logs a message without triggering a breakpoint. Intended to be called by the PS_LOG_WO_BREAK_LIMITED/UNLIMITED macros when a condition fails, passing the message, source file, line, and function name. Typically used with syslog-style priorities (e.g., LOG_DEBUG/LOG_INFO/LOG_WARNING). Return value semantics are not documented in this header (unknown).
requirements: pri must be a valid logging priority compatible with the system’s logging facility (e.g., syslog priorities such as LOG_DEBUG, LOG_INFO, LOG_WARNING).
p must point to a valid, null-terminated C string containing the log message.
f must point to a valid, null-terminated C string naming the source file (usually provided via __FILE__).
l should be the source line number associated with the log (usually provided via __LINE__).
m may be null (default) or, if provided, must point to a valid, null-terminated C string (often the function name, e.g., __FUNCTION__).
Thread-safety and error/return conventions are not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: GuardAndDbgLog::GuardAndDbgLog
functions.signature: GuardAndDbgLog::GuardAndDbgLog(const char *mtx_name, unsigned ln, const char *fn, std::mutex *mutex_ptr);
functions.description: Debug-only helper that records context about a mutex lock operation (mutex name, source line, source file, and the mutex address). It is constructed just before a lock is taken (as used by GUARD_AND_DBG_LOG), likely for diagnostic logging of lock acquisition and for aiding in debugging lock-related issues. Only available when DEBUG is defined.
requirements: Only available/compiled when DEBUG is defined; do not rely on it in release builds.
mtx_name must be a valid, null-terminated C string describing the mutex (e.g., the macro-stringized mutex variable name).
ln should be the source line number at which the lock is attempted (typically __LINE__).
fn must be a valid, null-terminated C string indicating the source file (as used by the macro, typically __FILE__).
mutex_ptr must point to a valid std::mutex whose lifetime extends at least through the lifetime of the GuardAndDbgLog instance.

functions.name: GuardAndDbgLog::~GuardAndDbgLog
functions.description: Debug-only destructor for GuardAndDbgLog. It likely finalizes any diagnostic logging related to the mutex lock scope (e.g., logging unlock or scope exit) to assist with debugging lock usage. Only available when DEBUG is defined.
requirements: Only available/compiled when DEBUG is defined; do not rely on it in release builds.
The associated GuardAndDbgLog instance must have been previously constructed with valid parameters (as per its constructor).
No exception-safety or error reporting behavior is documented in this header (unknown).

functions.name: PST_CLOCK_GETTIME
functions.signature: extern "C" int PST_CLOCK_GETTIME(PST_CLOCK_ID_T clockid, struct PST_TIMESPEC *tp);
functions.description: Windows compatibility wrapper for POSIX clock_gettime. Fills tp with the current time for the specified clockid (e.g., PST_CLOCK_REALTIME, PST_CLOCK_MONOTONIC) using Windows-under-the-hood implementations. Use this when building on Windows (_IS_WINDOWS defined) where native clock_gettime is unavailable.
requirements: Available only when _IS_WINDOWS is defined (Windows builds).
clockid must be a valid clock ID defined in winornix.h (e.g., PST_CLOCK_REALTIME, PST_CLOCK_MONOTONIC).
tp must be a non-null pointer to a writable PST_TIMESPEC structure.
On success, returns 0; on failure, returns -1 and follows the POSIX pattern of setting errno (inferred from naming and behavior of clock_gettime).

functions.name: PST_GMTIME_R
functions.signature: extern "C" struct tm *PST_GMTIME_R(const time_t *timep, struct tm *result);
functions.description: Windows compatibility wrapper for POSIX gmtime_r. Converts the time value pointed to by timep (seconds since the Epoch) to Coordinated Universal Time, storing the broken-down time in result. Thread-safe reentrant variant intended for Windows builds.
requirements: Available only when _IS_WINDOWS is defined (Windows builds).
timep must be a non-null pointer to a valid time_t value representing seconds since the Unix Epoch.
result must be a non-null pointer to a writable struct tm provided by the caller.
Returns result on success; returns NULL on failure and may set errno (pattern consistent with POSIX gmtime_r).

functions.name: PST_ASCTIME_R
functions.description: Windows compatibility wrapper for POSIX asctime_r. Formats the calendar time in tm into a human-readable ASCII string and stores it in the caller-provided buffer buf. Intended for use on Windows to provide a thread-safe asctime-like function.
requirements: Available only when _IS_WINDOWS is defined (Windows builds).
tm must be a non-null pointer to a valid struct tm representing a normalized calendar time (inferred from POSIX asctime_r usage).
buf must be a non-null pointer to a writable character buffer supplied by the caller.
Buffer size should be at least 26 bytes to hold the fixed-length asctime string including the terminating null (inferred from POSIX asctime_r).
Returns buf on success; returns NULL on failure and may set errno (pattern consistent with POSIX asctime_r).

functions.name: PST_LOCALTIME_R
functions.signature: extern "C" struct tm *PST_LOCALTIME_R(const time_t *timep, struct tm *result);
functions.description: Windows compatibility wrapper for POSIX localtime_r. Converts the time value pointed to by timep (seconds since the Epoch) to local time, storing the broken-down time in result. Thread-safe reentrant variant intended for Windows builds.
requirements: Available only when _IS_WINDOWS is defined (Windows builds).
timep must be a non-null pointer to a valid time_t value representing seconds since the Unix Epoch.
result must be a non-null pointer to a writable struct tm provided by the caller.
Returns result on success; returns NULL on failure and may set errno (pattern consistent with POSIX localtime_r).

functions.name: PST_FCNTL
functions.signature: extern "C" int PST_FCNTL(em_socket_t fd, int cmd, ...);
functions.description: Windows-specific fcntl-style helper for sockets. Provides a POSIX-like fcntl interface over an em_socket_t handle, intended to emulate or wrap fcntl behavior on Windows builds. Usage is analogous to fcntl(fd, cmd, arg?): pass a socket handle, a command, and optionally a command-specific argument via varargs. Supported commands, expected variadic argument types, return values, and error reporting are not documented here and should be confirmed in the corresponding implementation or library docs.
requirements: Available only when compiled on Windows builds where _IS_WINDOWS is defined; on other platforms this symbol may be unavailable.
fd must be a valid em_socket_t referring to an open socket/descriptor managed by this library.
cmd must be a command value recognized by PST_FCNTL; unsupported values are unspecified here.
If the chosen cmd requires an extra argument, supply exactly one additional variadic argument of the expected type for that command (types are unspecified here and must match the implementation).
Caller must ensure the lifetime of fd remains valid for the duration of the call.
Error/return-value conventions (e.g., -1 with errno set) are not documented here; callers should consult the implementation or test behavior before relying on specific error handling.

functions.name: PST_GETIFADDRS
functions.description: Windows-targeted counterpart to Linux getifaddrs. Allocates and returns a linked list of network interface entries (struct PST_IFADDRS) describing local interfaces (name, flags, addresses, netmask, and either broadcast or destination address). The list is linked via ifa_next. Intended usage mirrors getifaddrs: call PST_GETIFADDRS(&list), iterate the list, then release resources with PST_FREEIFADDRS(list). Return-value and errno conventions are not documented here; treat any nonzero return as an error unless the project’s documentation specifies otherwise.
requirements: Available only when _IS_WINDOWS is defined (function is declared within the _IS_WINDOWS section).
Parameter ifap must be a valid, non-null pointer to a struct PST_IFADDRS* (i.e., address of a pointer) where the function can store the head of the allocated list.
On success, the returned list and its internal memory (strings and socket address structures) must be released by calling PST_FREEIFADDRS with the head pointer; do not free with standard free/delete.

Callers should not assume any specific error-code or errno behavior on failure; they must check the integer return value and handle errors according to project conventions (details not specified in this header).
The returned list nodes are linked via the ifa_next field; iteration should follow this pointer until NULL.
Fields ifa_addr, ifa_netmask, and ifa_ifu.{ifu_broadaddr|ifu_dstaddr} are pointers that remain valid only until PST_FREEIFADDRS is called.

No thread-safety guarantees are stated; callers should avoid concurrent access to the returned list from multiple threads without external synchronization (inferred caution due to typical allocation semantics).

functions.name: PST_FREEIFADDRS
functions.description: Frees a list of interface entries previously allocated by PST_GETIFADDRS, including all associated dynamically allocated memory reachable from the list nodes. Use after finishing iteration/consumption of the interface list.
requirements: Argument ifa must be a pointer previously obtained from PST_GETIFADDRS (head of the list or a node from that allocation); do not pass arbitrary pointers.
Call exactly once for a given list returned by PST_GETIFADDRS; after freeing, all pointers into the list become invalid.
Do not use standard memory deallocation routines (free/delete) on the list; use this function exclusively.
Behavior for ifa == NULL is not specified in this header (caller should avoid passing NULL unless implementation confirms it is allowed).
Available only when _IS_WINDOWS is defined (function is declared within the _IS_WINDOWS section).

functions.name: pist_getrusage
functions.signature: extern "C" int pist_getrusage(int who, struct PST_RUSAGE *rusage)
functions.description: Windows-only (under _IS_WINDOWS) compatibility wrapper for POSIX getrusage. Fills a PST_RUSAGE structure with CPU time used (user time and system time) for the selected target (typically the current process or its children). Intended usage mirrors getrusage: pass a selector in who (e.g., PST_RUSAGE_SELF or PST_RUSAGE_CHILDREN from winornix.h) and a non-null pointer to a PST_RUSAGE to receive results. Only ru_utime and ru_stime are provided by PST_RUSAGE; other POSIX rusage fields are not available. Return convention is not documented here; by analogy to getrusage it likely returns 0 on success and -1 on error (with errno set), but this is inferred and not guaranteed.
requirements: Available only when compiled with _IS_WINDOWS defined; on non-Windows builds this function is not declared.
Include <pistache/winornix.h> before use so PST_RUSAGE_SELF and PST_RUSAGE_CHILDREN are defined; winsock2.h is required for struct timeval (transitively included here).
Argument who should be one of the supported selectors (inferred from comments: PST_RUSAGE_SELF or PST_RUSAGE_CHILDREN). Other values are unsupported/unspecified.
Parameter rusage must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable struct PST_RUSAGE.
Callers should not expect fields beyond ru_utime and ru_stime to be populated since PST_RUSAGE only contains those two fields.

Error handling behavior (return values and errno) is not specified in this header; callers should check the int return value and be prepared for nonzero/negative values to indicate failure (inferred from getrusage semantics).

functions.name: pist_sock_startup_check
functions.description: Initializes Winsock on Windows before any Winsock2 operations. It is idempotent and thread-safe; calls after the first do nothing. All pist_sock_* functions in this header call it internally; only needed explicitly if your code calls Winsock functions directly outside this wrapper.
requirements: Only available/compiled when _IS_WINDOWS is defined.
Should be called before any direct Winsock usage outside these pist_sock_* wrappers.
Returns 0 on success; returns -1 on failure with errno set. Callers must check the return value and handle errors.

functions.name: pist_sock_getsockname
functions.signature: int pist_sock_getsockname(em_socket_t em_sock, struct sockaddr *addr, PST_SOCKLEN_T *addrlen);
functions.description: Wrapper for getsockname on an em_socket_t. Fills in the local address bound to the socket.
requirements: Only available/compiled when _IS_WINDOWS is defined.
em_sock must be a valid, open socket (e.g., created by pist_sock_socket or returned by pist_sock_accept).
addr must point to a writable buffer for a sockaddr of sufficient size; addrlen must be non-null and point to a length variable.
Conventional getsockname semantics apply: on input *addrlen indicates the size of the buffer; on output it is set to the actual size used.
Returns 0 on success; returns -1 on failure with errno set. Callers must check and handle errors.

functions.name: pist_sock_close
functions.description: Closes an em_socket_t socket handle.
requirements: Only available/compiled when _IS_WINDOWS is defined.
em_sock must be a valid socket handle. Calling close on an invalid or already-closed socket is an error.
On success returns 0; on failure returns -1 with errno set. Callers must check and handle errors.
After a successful close, the socket must not be used again.

functions.name: pist_sock_read
functions.signature: PST_SSIZE_T pist_sock_read(em_socket_t em_sock, void *buf, size_t count);
functions.description: Reads up to count bytes from the socket into buf. Returns the number of bytes read, 0 on graceful connection close, or -1 on error (errno set).
requirements: Only available/compiled when _IS_WINDOWS is defined.
em_sock must be a valid, open socket.
buf must point to writable memory of at least count bytes.
count may be any size_t; short reads are possible.
Callers must handle return 0 as connection closed and -1 as error with errno set.

functions.name: pist_sock_write
functions.signature: PST_SSIZE_T pist_sock_write(em_socket_t em_sock, const void *buf, size_t count);
functions.description: Writes up to count bytes from buf to the socket. Returns the number of bytes written (which may be less than count), or -1 on error with errno set.
requirements: Only available/compiled when _IS_WINDOWS is defined.
em_sock must be a valid, open socket.
buf must point to readable memory of at least count bytes.
Callers must be prepared for partial writes even on success and should loop as needed to send all data.
On error returns -1 and sets errno; callers must check and handle errors.

functions.name: pist_sock_socket
functions.signature: em_socket_t pist_sock_socket(int domain, int type, int protocol);
functions.description: Creates a socket and returns its em_socket_t handle, or -1 on error with errno set. Wrapper around socket(domain,type,protocol).
requirements: Only available/compiled when _IS_WINDOWS is defined.
domain, type, and protocol must be valid for the platform (e.g., AF_*, SOCK_*, IPPROTO_*).
On failure returns -1 and sets errno; callers must check and handle errors before using the returned handle.

functions.name: pist_sock_bind
functions.signature: int pist_sock_bind(em_socket_t em_sock, const struct sockaddr *addr, PST_SOCKLEN_T addrlen);
functions.description: Binds the socket to a local address.
requirements: Only available/compiled when _IS_WINDOWS is defined.
em_sock must be a valid, unbound socket created by pist_sock_socket.
addr must point to a valid sockaddr for the specified address family; addrlen must match the size of the sockaddr structure.
Returns 0 on success; returns -1 on failure with errno set. Callers must check and handle errors.
Typically must be called before pist_sock_listen for server sockets.

functions.name: pist_sock_set_timeout
functions.signature: int pist_sock_set_timeout(em_socket_t em_sock, int optname, unsigned long int timeout_in_ms);
functions.description: Sets a socket I/O timeout (receive or send) in milliseconds via the given optname.
requirements: Only available/compiled when _IS_WINDOWS is defined.
em_sock must be a valid, open socket.
optname must be SO_RCVTIMEO or SO_SNDTIMEO (as stated in the header).
timeout_in_ms is specified in milliseconds; valid range is implementation-defined; negative values are not implied as valid by the header.
Returns 0 on success; returns -1 on failure with errno set. Callers must check and handle errors.

functions.name: pist_sock_accept
functions.signature: em_socket_t pist_sock_accept(em_socket_t em_sock, struct sockaddr *addr, PST_SOCKLEN_T *addrlen);
functions.description: Accepts a pending connection on a listening socket and returns a new em_socket_t for the accepted connection, or -1 on error with errno set. On success, optionally fills in the peer address.
requirements: Only available/compiled when _IS_WINDOWS is defined.
em_sock must be a valid socket in listening state (after pist_sock_listen).

If addr is provided, it must point to writable storage for a sockaddr; addrlen must be non-null and point to the buffer length, following standard accept semantics. If caller does not need the peer address, passing NULLs may be acceptable by standard patterns.
On failure returns -1 and sets errno; callers must check and handle errors.

functions.name: pist_sock_connect
functions.signature: int pist_sock_connect(em_socket_t em_sock, const struct sockaddr *addr, PST_SOCKLEN_T addrlen);
functions.description: Connects a socket to a remote address.
requirements: Only available/compiled when _IS_WINDOWS is defined.
em_sock must be a valid socket not already connected.
addr must point to a valid remote sockaddr; addrlen must match the structure size.
Returns 0 on success; returns -1 on failure with errno set. Callers must check and handle errors.

functions.name: pist_sock_listen
functions.description: Marks a bound socket as a passive (listening) socket that will accept incoming connections.
requirements: Only available/compiled when _IS_WINDOWS is defined.
em_sock must be a valid socket that has been successfully bound (pist_sock_bind).
backlog specifies the queue length; valid range is implementation-defined.
Returns 0 on success; returns -1 on failure with errno set. Callers must check and handle errors.
Must be called before pist_sock_accept to accept connections.

functions.name: pist_sock_send
functions.signature: PST_SSIZE_T pist_sock_send(em_socket_t em_sock, const void *buf, size_t len, int flags);
functions.description: Sends up to len bytes to a connected peer, honoring the specified flags. Returns number of bytes sent or -1 on error with errno set.
requirements: Only available/compiled when _IS_WINDOWS is defined.
em_sock must be a valid, open (typically connected) socket.
buf must point to readable memory of at least len bytes.
flags should be valid send/WSASend flags for the platform (e.g., MSG_*).
Partial sends may occur; callers should handle short returns.
On error returns -1 and sets errno; callers must check and handle errors.

functions.name: pist_sock_recv
functions.signature: PST_SSIZE_T pist_sock_recv(em_socket_t em_sock, void * buf, size_t len, int flags);
functions.description: Receives up to len bytes from a peer, honoring the specified flags. Returns number of bytes received, 0 on graceful close, or -1 on error with errno set.
requirements: Only available/compiled when _IS_WINDOWS is defined.
em_sock must be a valid, open socket.
buf must point to writable memory of at least len bytes.
flags should be valid recv/WSARecv flags for the platform (e.g., MSG_*).
Callers must handle 0 return as peer closed connection and -1 as error with errno set.

functions.name: pist_sock_select
functions.signature: int pist_sock_select(int nfds, fd_set * readfds, fd_set * writefds, fd_set * exceptfds, const struct timeval * timeout);
functions.description: Monitors multiple socket sets for readiness/readability, writability, or exceptional conditions until one becomes ready or the timeout expires. Returns the number of ready descriptors, 0 on timeout, or -1 on error with errno set.
requirements: Only available/compiled when _IS_WINDOWS is defined.
readfds, writefds, and exceptfds may be NULL if not used; when provided, they must be properly initialized fd_set structures containing sockets of interest.
timeout may be NULL (block indefinitely) or point to a timeval specifying the maximum wait time, following standard select semantics.
Return value semantics: >=0 indicates count of ready descriptors; -1 indicates error with errno set. Callers must check and handle errors.

functions.name: pist_sock_poll
functions.signature: int pist_sock_poll(PST_POLLFD_T * fds, PST_NFDS_T nfds, int timeout);
functions.description: Polls an array of sockets for events. On success returns the number of fds whose revents is nonzero, 0 on timeout, or -1 on error with errno set. Wrapper with poll-like semantics.
requirements: Only available/compiled when _IS_WINDOWS is defined.
fds must point to an array of at least nfds PST_POLLFD_T elements.
Each fds[i].fd must be a valid socket; fds[i].events must specify requested events; on return fds[i].revents is set.
nfds is the number of elements in the fds array; may be 0 to just sleep for timeout duration (by standard pattern).
timeout is in milliseconds; negative values conventionally mean wait indefinitely (pattern-based); exact supported range is implementation-defined.
Callers must check the return value and handle -1 with errno set.

functions.name: pist_strerror_r
functions.signature: extern "C" char * pist_strerror_r(int errnum, char *buf, size_t buflen);
functions.description: GNU/POSIX-style strerror_r wrapper intended for Windows (and some non-GNU environments). Converts an error number (errnum) into a human-readable message. Writes the error message into the provided buffer (buf) up to buflen bytes and returns a char* to the resulting message. Per GNU semantics, the returned pointer may be buf or may point to an internal static string. Use when you need a thread-friendly strerror variant with a caller-supplied buffer on platforms lacking GNU strerror_r. Exact error formatting, truncation behavior, and errno-setting are not documented here and may be implementation-dependent.
requirements: buf must be a valid, writable pointer to a buffer of at least buflen bytes.
buflen should be greater than 0 to allow space for a result and a terminating null character.
errnum should be a valid system error code for the target platform; behavior for unknown codes is implementation-defined/unknown.
Callers must not free the returned pointer unless it is equal to buf; if the returned pointer differs from buf, treat it as read-only and managed by the implementation (GNU strerror_r semantics).
Include <pistache/pist_strerror_r.h> and link against the library providing the implementation when used on platforms where this header enables the declaration.
This declaration is provided only when certain non-GNU platforms are detected via preprocessor checks; availability depends on build-time macros.

functions.name: PSLogFn
functions.signature: extern "C" void PSLogFn(int _pri, bool _andPrintf, const char *f, int l, const char *m, const char * _format, ...);
functions.description: Logs a formatted message at the given priority, including source location (file, line, and function). Intended to be used by the PS_LOG_* and PS_LOG_*_ARGS macros and to forward the message to syslog/unified logging and optionally stdout. The format string follows printf-style formatting and is paired with variadic arguments.
requirements: _pri should be one of the LOG_* priority constants (e.g., LOG_ALERT, LOG_ERR, LOG_WARNING, LOG_INFO, LOG_DEBUG).

_andPrintf controls echoing to stdout in addition to the platform log sink; actual behavior may also be influenced by the PS_LOG_AND_STDOUT define and, on Windows, by the Registry key HKCU:\Software\pistacheio\pistache property psLogToStdoutAsWell.
f must be a valid, null-terminated C string indicating the source file path (typically __FILE__).
l should be the source line number corresponding to f (typically __LINE__).
m must be a valid, null-terminated C string indicating the calling function name (typically __FUNCTION__).
_format must be a valid, null-terminated printf-style format string.
Variadic arguments must match the types and count required by _format; undefined behavior if mismatched.
Pointers passed (f, m, _format) must be non-null and point to accessible memory for the duration of the call.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unspecified/unknown from this header; callers should assume nothing unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: PSLogNoLocFn
functions.signature: extern "C" void PSLogNoLocFn(int _pri, bool _andPrintf, const char * _format, ...);
functions.description: Logs a formatted message at the given priority without attaching source location information. Used where file/line/function context is not available or desired. The format string follows printf-style formatting and is paired with variadic arguments.
requirements: _pri should be one of the LOG_* priority constants (e.g., LOG_ALERT, LOG_ERR, LOG_WARNING, LOG_INFO, LOG_DEBUG).

_andPrintf controls echoing to stdout in addition to the platform log sink; actual behavior may also be influenced by the PS_LOG_AND_STDOUT define and, on Windows, by the Registry key HKCU:\Software\pistacheio\pistache property psLogToStdoutAsWell.
_format must be a valid, null-terminated printf-style format string.
Variadic arguments must match the types and count required by _format; undefined behavior if mismatched.
_format must be non-null and point to accessible memory for the duration of the call.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unspecified/unknown from this header; callers should assume nothing unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: setPsLogCategory
functions.description: Sets the logging category/ident used by the underlying platform logger. On Linux/syslog: if called with a non-empty string before the first log, that string is passed as the ident to openlog; if called with NULL or an empty string, pistachio does not call openlog (the application may call openlog itself), or syslog may implicitly choose the executable name if logging occurs first. If not called, pistachio derives a 5-letter ident from the executable name at first log. On Apple unified logging, a non-empty category is used directly; otherwise a 5-letter category derived from the executable name is used when first logging. Calling this function is optional.
requirements: _category may be NULL, an empty string, or a non-empty null-terminated C string.
To ensure the provided category/ident is used by the platform logger, call this function before any logging occurs.

If using syslog and you want to control openlog yourself, either call this with NULL/empty before any pistachio logging and then call openlog manually, or call openlog before any pistachio logging happens.
Behavior differs by platform as documented; callers should not assume identical effects across Linux and Apple platforms.

functions.name: PSLogOss::PSLogOss
functions.description: Default constructor for PSLogOss, a helper that exposes ostream-like endpoints (debug, info, warning, error, alert) for stream-style logging via macros like PSLG_DEBUG_OS << .... Implementation is not provided in this header; it likely initializes the internal ostream members to route output to the logging backend.
requirements: Class must be linked with a definition of PSLogOss::PSLogOss; only the declaration is present in this header.
Construction requires no arguments.
Semantics of the ostream members (buffering, flushing, thread-safety) are unspecified/unknown from this header.

functions.name: __PS_TIMEDBG::__PS_TIMEDBG
functions.signature: __PS_TIMEDBG::__PS_TIMEDBG(char marker_ch, const char *f, int l, const char *m, const char *_inf)
functions.description: RAII constructor that starts a timing/logging scope. On construction it records wall and CPU times, computes a thread-local call depth marker, and logs a “start” message (optionally including an info string) via PSLogFn. Intended usage: create a stack instance (often through the PS_TIMEDBG_START* macros) at the beginning of a block/function to automatically log entry and, on destruction, elapsed time.
requirements: Available only when PS_TIMINGS_DBG is defined before including this header; otherwise the class is not defined.
Parameters f and m must point to valid, null-terminated C strings (typically __FILE__ and __FUNCTION__).
Parameter l is the source line number (typically __LINE__).
Parameter _inf may be nullptr; if non-null it must point to a valid, null-terminated C string.
Construction performs time queries; there is no caller-visible error reporting.

functions.name: __PS_TIMEDBG::~__PS_TIMEDBG
functions.description: RAII destructor that ends the timing/logging scope. It captures current wall and CPU times, computes elapsed time vs. the constructor’s timestamps, formats a closing marker based on thread-local nesting depth, and logs an “end” message including the elapsed time and the per-instance counter.
requirements: Available only when PS_TIMINGS_DBG is defined before including this header.
Object must have been successfully constructed before destruction (standard C++ object lifetime rules).
Destructor has no parameters and does not throw; callers do not need to perform error handling.

functions.name: __PS_TIMEDBG::getCounter
functions.description: Returns the per-instance counter value assigned at construction time. Useful to correlate start and end log messages for the same __PS_TIMEDBG instance.
requirements: Available only when PS_TIMINGS_DBG is defined before including this header.
May be called any time after construction and before destruction of the same instance.

functions.name: __PS_TIMEDBG::getInf
functions.signature: static const char * __PS_TIMEDBG::getInf(char *_buff, unsigned _buffSize, const char *_format, ...)
functions.description: Utility formatter for optional info strings used in timing logs. Writes a formatted string into the caller-provided buffer using printf-style formatting and returns a pointer to the buffer. If the formatted output would not fit, it truncates and appends "...". Returns nullptr if inputs are invalid.
requirements: Available only when PS_TIMINGS_DBG is defined before including this header.
_format must not be nullptr; if it is nullptr the function returns nullptr.
_buff must not be nullptr and _buffSize must be at least 6; otherwise the function returns nullptr.
The variadic arguments must match _format as in printf-family functions; undefined behavior if mismatched.
The returned pointer aliases _buff; the caller must ensure _buff remains valid for the duration of use.
If the formatted output length is >= (_buffSize - 6), the content is truncated and suffixed with "...".

functions.name: Pistache::Prototype::~Prototype
functions.description: Virtual defaulted destructor of the Prototype interface. Enables safe polymorphic deletion of objects implementing the Prototype<Class> interface.
requirements: May be invoked polymorphically; base class has a virtual destructor, so deleting via a Prototype<Class>* is valid.
No arguments and no return value; it performs default destruction of the object state.
No additional preconditions are specified; thread-safety and side effects are unknown.

functions.name: Pistache::Prototype::clone
functions.signature:
template <typename Class>
virtual std::shared_ptr<Class> clone() const = 0;
functions.description: Pure-virtual cloning interface that returns a heap-allocated copy of the current object as a std::shared_ptr<Class>. Implement this in derived classes to support the Prototype pattern. Typical usage is to call clone() on a Base pointer/reference to obtain a polymorphic copy.
requirements: Must be called on an object of a concrete class that derives from Prototype<Class> and overrides clone().
Override must return a new object that is logically an independent copy of *this wrapped in std::shared_ptr<Class>.

If the provided PROTOTYPE_OF(Base, Class) macro is used to implement clone(), the derived Class must be copy-constructible (the macro performs std::make_shared<Class>(*this)) and publicly override Base::clone().
Function is const; implementations must not mutate observable state of the source object when cloning.
Error handling/exception guarantees are unspecified; callers should assume clone() may throw if allocation or copying fails (inferred from use of std::make_shared and copy construction).

functions.name: ps_basename_r
functions.signature: extern "C" char * ps_basename_r(const char * path, char * bname);
functions.description: Re-entrant basename helper: extracts the last path component from the null-terminated C string path and writes it into the caller-provided buffer bname, then returns a pointer to the resulting basename. Intended as a portable replacement where a native basename_r is unavailable. Exact edge-case semantics (e.g., handling of trailing slashes or empty strings) are not documented here and may follow common basename conventions; details are unknown from this header.
requirements: path must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer.
bname must be a valid, writable buffer pointer.

bname should be large enough to hold the resulting basename plus a terminating NUL; by convention with basename_r, this is typically at least PST_MAXPATHLEN bytes (PST_MAXPATHLEN is referenced via the included PST_MAXPATH_HDR).
The function is intended to be re-entrant/thread-safe by using a caller-provided buffer.
Return/error conventions (e.g., whether NULL can be returned on error) are not specified in this header and are unknown.

functions.name: PS_BASENAME_R
functions.signature: char * PS_BASENAME_R(const char * path, char * bname);
functions.description: Thread-safe (reentrant) basename utility. On Apple platforms it aliases to basename_r; on other platforms it aliases to ps_basename_r (provided by this library). It extracts the final path component from path and writes it into the caller-provided buffer bname, returning a pointer to the resulting string. Expected usage: pass a null-terminated file system path and a writable buffer; the function copies the last component (without directory prefixes) into the buffer and null-terminates it. Notes: the API does not take a buffer size parameter, so the caller must ensure bname is large enough for the result; PST_MAXPATHLEN is made available by this header for sizing, but exact limits or truncation behavior are not documented here. Error/edge-case behavior (empty strings, trailing slashes, root-only paths, nullptr inputs) is not documented in this header and may vary by platform; callers should defensively validate inputs.
requirements: path must be a valid, non-null, null-terminated C string representing a file system path.
bname must be non-null and point to writable memory sufficient to hold the basename plus a terminating '\0'.

Because no size parameter is provided, the function assumes the buffer is large enough; using a buffer sized at least PST_MAXPATHLEN bytes is implied by this header’s inclusion of PST_MAXPATHLEN, though exact minimum is not specified.
The function may be called from multiple threads; it is intended to be reentrant and should not rely on internal static storage.

Return value is expected to be a pointer to the resulting string (typically bname); specific error indications (e.g., returning nullptr) are not specified in this header and should be handled conservatively by the caller.

functions.name: ps_sendfile
functions.signature: extern "C" PST_SSIZE_T ps_sendfile(em_socket_t out_fd, int in_fd, off_t *offset, size_t count);
functions.description: Linux-style sendfile implementation exposed for platforms that do not provide it natively (Windows, BSD). Transfers up to count bytes from the file referred to by in_fd to the socket out_fd, starting at the file position specified by *offset if non-null, otherwise using the file descriptor’s current offset. Returns a signed byte count (PST_SSIZE_T) similar to ssize_t. Use when you need to send file data directly to a socket without a userspace copy on non-Linux systems.
requirements: out_fd must be a valid em_socket_t representing a writable socket.
in_fd must be a valid file descriptor for a readable regular file.
If offset is non-null, *offset is the starting file offset and will be advanced by the number of bytes sent; if null, the file’s current offset is used and advanced.
count should be the maximum number of bytes to send; must fit in size_t.
The function returns a signed byte count; callers must check for negative values to detect errors and consult errno (conventional Linux sendfile semantics).
Thread-safety and signal-interruption behavior are unspecified here; callers should be prepared for partial transfers and to retry as appropriate.

functions.name: ::sendfile
functions.signature: ssize_t ::sendfile(int out_fd, int in_fd, off_t *offset, size_t count);
functions.description: Linux variant of sendfile (exposed when compiling on Linux). Transfers up to count bytes from the file in_fd to the socket out_fd, starting at *offset if non-null, or at the file descriptor’s current offset if null. Returns the number of bytes written, or -1 on error. Intended for zero-copy file-to-socket transfers.
requirements: out_fd must be a valid file descriptor referring to a socket opened for writing.
in_fd must be a valid file descriptor referring to a regular file opened for reading.
If offset is non-null, *offset supplies the starting read position and is updated by the number of bytes sent; if null, the kernel uses and updates the file’s current offset.
count must be a non-negative size not exceeding the file size and should fit within size_t.
Callers must handle short writes (partial transfers) and check for a return value of -1 to detect errors and inspect errno.

functions.name: PS_SENDFILE
functions.signature: PST_SSIZE_T PS_SENDFILE(em_socket_t out_fd, int in_fd, off_t *offset, size_t count);
functions.description: Cross-platform alias for a Linux-style sendfile on Windows and BSD. This emulation function transfers up to count bytes from a file descriptor (in_fd) to a socket-like handle (out_fd), optionally using and updating the file offset via offset. Intended to mimic Linux sendfile semantics for platforms that lack a native compatible API.
requirements: out_fd must be a valid em_socket_t referring to a writable socket-like endpoint.
in_fd must be a valid file descriptor opened for reading.
offset points to an off_t that may be used/updated by the transfer; Linux-style semantics are intended, but exact nullability and update behavior are not documented here.
count specifies the maximum number of bytes to transfer; must be representable as size_t.
The return type PST_SSIZE_T indicates a byte-count or error; exact error signaling is platform/implementation dependent (likely negative on error) and not documented in this header.

functions.name: ps_strlcpy
functions.signature: extern "C" size_t ps_strlcpy(char *dst, const char *src, size_t size);
functions.description: Portable, BSD-style string copy. Copies a C string from src into dst with a total destination buffer capacity of size bytes, writing at most size-1 characters and NUL-terminating the result when size > 0. Intended as a drop-in replacement for strlcpy on platforms that lack it. Return value is typically the length of src; callers can detect truncation when the return value >= size. Behavior details are inferred from BSD strlcpy semantics based on the header comment; exact edge-case behavior is otherwise not documented here.
requirements: dst must point to writable memory that can hold at least size bytes (inferred from BSD strlcpy and the size parameter semantics).
src must point to a NUL-terminated C string (inferred from BSD strlcpy).
size specifies the full capacity of dst including space for the terminating NUL; size may be 0 (inferred from BSD strlcpy).
Buffers must not overlap (typical requirement for string copy functions; inferred).
To detect truncation, compare the return value with size: truncation if return >= size (inferred).

functions.name: ps_strlcat
functions.signature: extern "C" size_t ps_strlcat(char *dst, const char *src, size_t size);
functions.description: Portable, BSD-style string concatenation. Appends src to the end of dst while ensuring the total size of the buffer referenced by dst is size bytes, writing at most size-1 total characters and NUL-terminating when possible. Intended as a drop-in replacement for strlcat on platforms that lack it. Return value is typically the length of the string it tried to create (initial length of dst plus length of src); callers can detect truncation when the return value >= size. Behavior details are inferred from BSD strlcat semantics based on the header comment; exact edge-case behavior is otherwise not documented here.
requirements: dst must point to a writable NUL-terminated C string stored in a buffer of at least size bytes (inferred from BSD strlcat).
src must point to a NUL-terminated C string (inferred).
size specifies the full capacity of the dst buffer including space for the terminating NUL (inferred).
Buffers must not overlap (typical requirement for string concatenation; inferred).
To detect truncation, compare the return value with size: truncation if return >= size (inferred).

functions.name: ps_strncpy_s
functions.signature: extern "C" int ps_strncpy_s(char *strDest, size_t numberOfElements, const char *strSource, size_t count);
functions.description: Safe bounded string copy with errno-based error reporting. Copies up to count characters from strSource into strDest, where strDest has capacity for numberOfElements characters. On success returns 0. On failure returns -1 and sets errno; if the copy would result in truncation, errno is set to PS_ESTRUNCATE. This function intentionally differs from C Annex K strncpy_s by returning int and using errno (to avoid errno_t dependency). Exact NUL-termination and other Annex K constraints are not documented here and thus remain unknown.
requirements: strDest must point to writable memory with capacity for at least numberOfElements bytes/characters.
strSource must point to a readable string; expected to be a C string, but exact requirements (e.g., allowance of nulls within count) are unknown.

count is the maximum number of characters to copy; if copying count characters would not fit within numberOfElements without truncation, the function fails with -1 and sets errno to PS_ESTRUNCATE (explicitly documented truncation behavior).
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates failure with errno set (explicit).
The exact NUL-termination behavior on success or failure is not specified in this header and should not be assumed (unknown).
Overlapping strDest and strSource is not documented; avoid overlap to prevent undefined behavior (inferred).

template <typename T, size_t N>
static Pistache::View<T> Pistache::impl::ViewBuilder<T (&)[N]>::buildSize(T (&arr)[N], size_t size)
functions.description: Builds a non-owning view over the first size elements of a native C array T[N]. Throws std::invalid_argument if size > N.
requirements: size must be <= N; otherwise std::invalid_argument is thrown.
arr must remain alive for the lifetime of the resulting view.
Callers should be prepared to catch std::invalid_argument when providing an out-of-bounds size.

functions.name: Pistache::details::unreachable
functions.description: Marks a code path as unreachable, enabling compiler optimizations and, on supported compilers, acting as a no-return hint. Implemented as an alias to std::unreachable when available, otherwise via compiler intrinsics (__builtin_unreachable on GCC/Clang, __assume(false) on MSVC), and as a no-op fallback on unknown compilers. Intended use: place at points the program must never reach (e.g., after exhaustive switch statements, default cases that are logically impossible). Note: on most platforms this function will not return if executed; on unsupported compilers it may be a no-op and return normally.
requirements: Call only in code paths that are logically unreachable; executing it in reachable code results in undefined behavior on compilers where it maps to non-returning intrinsics.
Do not rely on this function to terminate control flow: on some compilers (fallback implementation) it may be a no-op and return normally.
No arguments; no side effects guaranteed beyond compiler assumptions; ensure any required runtime termination (e.g., abort/throw) is performed separately if needed.
Fully qualify the name or use the Pistache::details namespace to call it.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target format: generic string used across many stubs as:
# - HTTP header values (Accept, Content-Type, Authorization parts)
# - Cookie name/value, raw cookie header
# - URL paths, hostnames, query params
# - Base64 encoder input and Basic auth credentials
# - Logging messages, filenames
# We generate a single bytes buffer that the harness will split as needed.
# Since FUZZ_PARAM_STR returns an arbitrary std::string, we craft a corpus-like
# sequence of concatenated strings separated by newlines so that consumers that
# read once or many times still see varied, valid tokens.

SAFE_TOKENS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-._~"
HEADER_TOKENS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-._;=, /+*"  # for header fields
URL_TOKENS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-._~/?:#[]@!$&'()*+,;=%"
B64TOKENS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "+/="


def _rand_rng(r: random.Random, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
    return r.randint(lo, hi)


def _rand_token(r: random.Random, alphabet: str, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = _rand_rng(r, min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _gen_host(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix host forms: domain, ipv4, ipv6-literal
    choice = r.randint(0, 4)
    if choice == 0:
        # simple domain
        labels = [_rand_token(r, string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits, 1, 10) for _ in range(r.randint(2, 4))]
        return ".".join(labels)
    if choice == 1:
        # domain with hyphens
        label = _rand_token(r, string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-", 1, 12).strip("-") or "host"
        tld = r.choice(["com", "net", "org", "io", "local"])
        return f"{label}.{tld}"
    if choice == 2:
        # ipv4
        return ".".join(str(r.randint(0, 255)) for _ in range(4))
    if choice == 3:
        # ipv6 literal
        parts = [format(r.getrandbits(16), 'x') for _ in range(8)]
        return f"[{'::'.join(parts[:1]) if r.random()<0.3 else ':'.join(parts)}]"
    # path-like host (to exercise AddressParser unix path branch)
    return "/tmp/" + _rand_token(r, SAFE_TOKENS, 1, 10)


def _gen_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    segs = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 5)):
        seg = _rand_token(r, SAFE_TOKENS, 1, 12)
        segs.append(seg)
    return "/" + "/".join(segs)


def _gen_query(r: random.Random) -> str:
    pairs: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 4)):
        k = _rand_token(r, string.ascii_lowercase, 1, 8)
        v = _rand_token(r, SAFE_TOKENS, 0, 10)
        pairs.append(f"{k}={v}")
    return "?" + "&".join(pairs)


def _gen_cookie_raw(r: random.Random) -> str:
    name = _rand_token(r, string.ascii_letters + string.digits, 1, 10)
    val = _rand_token(r, SAFE_TOKENS, 0, 12)
    attrs = []
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        attrs.append(f"Path=/{_rand_token(r, SAFE_TOKENS, 0, 6)}")
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        attrs.append(f"Domain={_gen_host(r)}")
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        attrs.append("HttpOnly")
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        attrs.append("Secure")
    return "; ".join([f"{name}={val}"] + attrs)


def _gen_mime(r: random.Random) -> str:
    top = r.choice(["application", "text", "image", "audio", "video"])
    sub = _rand_token(r, string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-", 3, 10)
    parts = [f"{top}/{sub}"]
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        parts.append(f"charset={r.choice(['utf-8','iso-8859-1','us-ascii'])}")
    return "; ".join(parts)


def _gen_basic_auth_header(r: random.Random) -> str:
    user = _rand_token(r, SAFE_TOKENS, 1, 12)
    pw = _rand_token(r, SAFE_TOKENS, 0, 12)
    raw = f"{user}:{pw}".encode('utf-8')
    # Manual base64 to avoid external deps
    b64_table = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/"
    out = bytearray()
    i = 0
    while i < len(raw):
        block = raw[i:i+3]
        i += 3
        b0 = block[0]
        b1 = block[1] if len(block) > 1 else 0
        b2 = block[2] if len(block) > 2 else 0
        out.append(b64_table[(b0 >> 2) & 0x3F])
        out.append(b64_table[((b0 & 0x03) << 4) | ((b1 >> 4) & 0x0F)])
        if len(block) > 1:
            out.append(b64_table[((b1 & 0x0F) << 2) | ((b2 >> 6) & 0x03)])
        else:
            out.append(ord('='))
        if len(block) > 2:
            out.append(b64_table[b2 & 0x3F])
        else:
            out.append(ord('='))
    return "Basic " + out.decode('ascii')


def _gen_accept_encoding(r: random.Random) -> str:
    encs = ["gzip", "deflate", "br", "zstd", "identity"]
    vals = []
    for e in r.sample(encs, k=r.randint(1, min(3, len(encs)))):
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            q = r.randint(0, 100) / 100.0
            vals.append(f"{e};q={q:.2f}")
        else:
            vals.append(e)
    return ", ".join(vals)


def _gen_user_agent(r: random.Random) -> str:
    prod = _rand_token(r, string.ascii_letters, 3, 8)
    ver = f"{r.randint(0,99)}.{r.randint(0,9)}"
    sys = r.choice(["Windows NT 10.0", "Linux x86_64", "Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 14_0"])
    return f"Mozilla/5.0 ({sys}) {prod}/{ver}"


def _gen_swagger_pathish(r: random.Random) -> str:
    p = _gen_path(r)
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        p += _gen_query(r)
    return p


def _gen_base64_input(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Return raw text that is safe to base64-encode by the library later
    return _rand_token(r, ''.join(chr(i) for i in range(32, 127)), 0, 64)


def _gen_filename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base = _rand_token(r, SAFE_TOKENS, 1, 12)
    ext = r.choice([".txt", ".json", ".pem", ".key", ".log"]) if r.random() < 0.7 else ""
    prefix = r.choice(["/tmp/", "/var/tmp/", "C:/tmp/"])
    return prefix + base + ext


def _sections(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Compose a diverse set of strings, each on its own line.
    items: List[str] = []
    items.append(_gen_host(r))                           # host
    items.append(_gen_path(r))                           # path
    items.append(_gen_swagger_pathish(r))                # swagger-ish path with query
    items.append(_gen_cookie_raw(r))                     # raw cookie header
    items.append(_gen_mime(r))                           # content-type
    items.append(_gen_accept_encoding(r))                # accept-encoding
    items.append(_gen_user_agent(r))                     # user-agent
    items.append(_gen_basic_auth_header(r))              # Authorization: Basic ...
    items.append(_rand_token(r, HEADER_TOKENS, 0, 64))   # generic header value
    items.append(_rand_token(r, URL_TOKENS, 0, 64))      # url-ish token
    items.append(_gen_base64_input(r))                   # base64-encodable input
    items.append(_gen_filename(r))                       # filename
    # Cookie name/value singular
    items.append(_rand_token(r, string.ascii_letters+string.digits, 1, 10))
    items.append(_rand_token(r, SAFE_TOKENS, 0, 12))
    # Query key/value small
    items.append(_rand_token(r, string.ascii_lowercase, 1, 8))
    items.append(_rand_token(r, SAFE_TOKENS, 0, 10))
    # General messages for errors/logging
    items.append(_rand_token(r, string.printable.replace("\n", " "), 0, 80).strip())
    items.append(_rand_token(r, string.printable.replace("\n", " "), 0, 120).strip())
    return items


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Build multiple groups to ensure buffers have plenty of material
    groups = r.randint(2, 5)
    lines: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(groups):
        lines.extend(_sections(r))
    # Ensure total size <= 4096 bytes
    blob = ("\n".join(lines))[:4096]
    return blob.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')

import random
import base64
import os
from typing import List

# Target: Generate valid Base64-encoded strings that exercise
# - Base64Decoder constructed with a backing std::string (length multiple of 4 preferred)
# - Authorization::parse expecting "Basic <base64(user:pass)>" with user:pass round-trip
# The fuzzer stub will obtain data via FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME. Our single
# bytes buffer should be a textual payload; the harness will slice it as needed.

# We emit one Base64 string per call. To increase variety while remaining valid,
# we choose among several interesting decoded payload shapes and then base64-encode.

_MAX_OUT = 4096

SAFE_ASCII = bytes([c for c in range(32, 127)])


def _rand(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))


def _gen_userpass(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a user:pass pair with varied characters but reasonable sizes (<=32)
    # Keep them ASCII-safe for predictable round-trip.
    user_len = rng.randint(0, 32)
    pass_len = rng.randint(0, 32)
    user = _rand(rng, user_len).decode('ascii', 'ignore')
    pw = _rand(rng, pass_len).decode('ascii', 'ignore')
    return f"{user}:{pw}"


def _choose_plain_payloads(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create a mix of payloads that are interesting for Base64 decode paths
    choices: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Empty
    choices.append(b"")

    # 2) Short ASCII
    choices.append(b"A")
    choices.append(b"AB")
    choices.append(b"ABC")
    choices.append(b"Hello, World!")

    # 3) Binary-like content covering all byte values in small chunks
    choices.append(bytes(range(0, 64)))
    choices.append(bytes(range(64, 128)))

    # 4) Repeated patterns
    pat = b"\x00\xff\x7fABC"
    choices.append(pat * rng.randint(1, 20))

    # 5) Random sized (0..1500) with ASCII-safe content so it’s printable if used in headers
    choices.append(_rand(rng, rng.randint(0, 1500)))

    # 6) user:pass form for Authorization Basic
    choices.append(_gen_userpass(rng).encode('ascii', 'ignore'))

    # 7) JSON-like text
    choices.append(b'{"k":"v","n":123,"b":true}')

    # 8) Long text with newlines (base64 is resilient to newlines in some decoders, but
    # we keep only in decoded data; encoding will produce base64 without newlines)
    choices.append((b"line1\nline2\n" * rng.randint(1, 50)))

    return rng.choice(choices)


def _encode_b64(data: bytes) -> str:
    # Standard base64 without newlines, padding included by default
    return base64.b64encode(data).decode('ascii')


def _maybe_wrap_as_basic(rng: random.Random, b64: str) -> str:
    # Sometimes produce a full Authorization header value for the parser stub
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return f"Basic {b64}"
    return b64


def _maybe_add_whitespace_variants(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Occasionally add surrounding spaces or trailing newline to exercise parse trimming
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        left = "" if rng.random() < 0.5 else " " * rng.randint(1, 3)
        right = "" if rng.random() < 0.5 else (" " * rng.randint(1, 3))
        s = f"{left}{s}{right}"
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        s = s + "\n"
    return s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide strategy
    mode = rng.random()

    if mode < 0.4:
        # Focus on Authorization Basic with valid user:pass
        up = _gen_userpass(rng).encode('ascii', 'ignore')
        b64 = _encode_b64(up)
        out = _maybe_wrap_as_basic(rng, b64)
    elif mode < 0.8:
        # Generic base64 from interesting payloads
        payload = _choose_plain_payloads(rng)
        out = _encode_b64(payload)
        # Occasionally prefix with "Basic " to hit Authorization path too
        out = _maybe_wrap_as_basic(rng, out)
    else:
        # Large payload near limits, still valid base64
        size = rng.randint(1800, 3000)
        payload = _rand(rng, size)
        out = _encode_b64(payload)

    out = _maybe_add_whitespace_variants(rng, out)

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(out) > _MAX_OUT:
        out = out[:_MAX_OUT]

    return out.encode('ascii', 'ignore')

import random
from typing import List

# Data type: arbitrary binary (as bytes)
# Targets use FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME. Our generator returns a
# single bytes buffer that the harness will use to seed those sources. We want
# valid and interesting data for:
# - Base64Encoder input buffer (raw bytes of varying sizes)
# - HTTP parsers and headers expecting textual HTTP-like data
# - MIME MediaType::fromFile (filename with extension)
# - ArrayStreamBuf::feed, StreamCursor parsing helpers (need newlines, spaces, tokens)
# - Authorization header (exercise Basic and Bearer forms)
# - make_view over strings/vectors (size variety)
# The buffer should stay <= 4096 bytes.
# Strategy: Build a multi-section blob containing:
# 1) Several Base64-like chunks (valid Base64 strings and random bytes)
# 2) A realistic HTTP request and response with headers (Content-Type, Accept-Encoding,
#    Transfer-Encoding: chunked, Cookie, ETag, Authorization: Basic/Bearer)
# 3) Random binary segment for RawBuffer/FileBuffer data
# 4) Filenames with various extensions to exercise MediaType::fromFile
# 5) Small literals and delimiter-rich lines for StreamCursor tests
# 6) A trailing null byte to ensure non-empty buffers where required
# Sections are separated with newlines to support line-oriented consumers.

_B64_ALPH = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/"

def _rand_base64_chunk(rng: random.Random, with_padding: bool) -> bytes:
    # Create random 1-60 bytes, encode manually into valid base64 string characters,
    # but we are not required to encode; many consumers only need plausible base64 text.
    # We'll generate a random valid-looking base64 with optional '=' padding.
    n = rng.randint(4, 120)
    # ensure multiple of 4 length if padding requested
    if with_padding:
        n = (n // 4) * 4 or 4
    s = bytes(rng.choice(_B64_ALPH) for _ in range(n))
    if with_padding and n >= 4:
        # randomly add '=' padding at the end (0-2)
        pad = rng.randint(0, 2)
        if pad:
            s = s[:-pad] + b"=" * pad
    return s

def _http_request(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    methods = [b"GET", b"POST", b"PUT", b"PATCH", b"DELETE", b"HEAD", b"OPTIONS"]
    path_opts = [b"/", b"/index.html", b"/api/v1/items?x=1&y=2", b"/upload", b"/chunk"]
    method = rng.choice(methods)
    path = rng.choice(path_opts)
    ver = rng.choice([b"HTTP/1.1", b"HTTP/1.0"])  # request-line
    lines: List[bytes] = []
    lines.append(method + b" " + path + b" " + ver)
    # Common headers
    host = b"example.com" if rng.random() < 0.7 else b"localhost"
    lines.append(b"Host: " + host)
    # Accept-Encoding exercises parser of q-values; include a couple
    lines.append(b"Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br; q=0.7, zstd; q=0.6")
    # Content-Type with parameters
    cts = rng.choice([b"text/plain; charset=utf-8", b"application/json", b"application/xml", b"application/octet-stream"])
    lines.append(b"Content-Type: " + cts)
    # Authorization: both Basic and Bearer variants
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # Basic dXNlcjpwYXNz (user:pass)
        lines.append(b"Authorization: Basic dXNlcjpwYXNz")
    else:
        lines.append(b"Authorization: Bearer abcdef0123456789")
    # Cookies
    lines.append(b"Cookie: sid=abc123; theme=light; sessionToken=xyz")
    # Transfer-Encoding sometimes chunked
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        lines.append(b"Transfer-Encoding: chunked")
        body = b"\r\n".join(lines) + b"\r\n\r\n"
        # Add a small valid chunked body
        chunks = [b"4\r\nWiki\r\n", b"5\r\npedia\r\n", b"0\r\n\r\n"]
        return body + b"".join(chunks)
    else:
        payload = b"Hello World" * rng.randint(1, 5)
        lines.append(b"Content-Length: " + str(len(payload)).encode())
        body = b"\r\n".join(lines) + b"\r\n\r\n" + payload
        return body

def _http_response(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    ver = rng.choice([b"HTTP/1.1", b"HTTP/1.0"])  # status-line
    status = rng.choice([(200, b"OK"), (204, b"No Content"), (301, b"Moved Permanently"), (400, b"Bad Request"), (404, b"Not Found")])
    code, msg = status
    lines: List[bytes] = []
    lines.append(ver + b" " + str(code).encode() + b" " + msg)
    lines.append(b"Server: Pistache-Test/0.1")
    lines.append(b"Date: Sat, 01 Jan 2000 00:00:00 GMT")
    lines.append(b"ETag: \"abc123\"")
    lines.append(b"Connection: keep-alive")
    if code in (204, 301):
        lines.append(b"Content-Length: 0")
        return b"\r\n".join(lines) + b"\r\n\r\n"
    body = rng.choice([b"{}", b"<ok/>", b"OK", b"response body\nwith newline"]) 
    ctype = rng.choice([b"application/json", b"text/plain", b"text/html; charset=utf-8"]) 
    lines.append(b"Content-Type: " + ctype)
    lines.append(b"Content-Length: " + str(len(body)).encode())
    return b"\r\n".join(lines) + b"\r\n\r\n" + body

def _filenames_block(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Provide multiple filenames separated by newlines; FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME may pick one
    names = [
        b"sample.txt", b"image.png", b"photo.jpg", b"doc.pdf", b"archive.tar.gz",
        b"data.json", b"index.html", b"script.js", b"style.css", b"bin.dat"
    ]
    # also add a path-like entry
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        names.append(b"/tmp/fuzz_input.bin")
    return b"\n".join(names) + b"\n"

def _delim_rich_lines(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Lines with spaces, tabs, commas, semicolons to exercise match_until and token logic
    samples = [
        b"alpha beta\tgamma,delta;epsilon\n",
        b"line1\nline2\r\nline3\n",
        b"key: value; another=pair, and\tmore\n",
    ]
    # Add a line starting with a likely literal to match
    samples.append(b"L start-with-L literal\n")
    return b"".join(samples)

def _random_binary(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(32, max_len)
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Base64-like segments
    for _ in range(3):
        parts.append(_rand_base64_chunk(rng, with_padding=rng.random() < 0.7))
        parts.append(b"\n")

    # 2) HTTP request and response blocks
    parts.append(_http_request(rng))
    parts.append(b"\n\n")
    parts.append(_http_response(rng))
    parts.append(b"\n\n")

    # 3) Filenames for fromFile consumers
    parts.append(_filenames_block(rng))

    # 4) Delimiter-rich lines for StreamCursor helpers
    parts.append(_delim_rich_lines(rng))

    # 5) Random binary region for RawBuffer/FileBuffer
    parts.append(_random_binary(rng, 512))

    # 6) Another small HTTP-like snippet to increase coverage
    parts.append(b"GET /small HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: a\r\nContent-Length: 1\r\n\r\nX")

    blob = b"".join(parts)

    # Ensure there is at least one null byte near the end to exercise edge cases
    blob += b"\x00"

    # Limit to 4096 bytes
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        blob = blob[:4096]

    return blob
